# Build guide

> Build a Svalboard from a self-print kit, from printing the parts to the first fit.

![A finished Svalboard in gray and black on a white background: both halves, each with four finger clusters, a thumb cluster, a black trackball and a gray hemispherical palm rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/finished-svalboard.tHKSbH7k_1ChByM.webp)

A finished board

![The kit hardware laid out on a white background: FFCs, the two main PCBAs, cluster and thumb PCBAs, stainless towers, screws, square nuts, brass heat set inserts, two rods of magnets, a T10 driver and two USB-C cables.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/kit-hardware-photo.CEjfYeSS_1xOtAB.webp)

What comes in the kit

This guide covers building a Svalboard from a self-print kit. It also helps with repairs and part swaps on a finished board.

Help us improve it: [open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/svalboard/docs/issues/new?title=Build%20guide%3A%20), or send comments on the [Svalboard Discord](https://www.svalboard.com/discord).

* Before you print, pick your key size. See [Sizing before you build](/build/#sizing-before-you-build).
* To configure your Svalboard after the build, use [Keybard](/keybard/) in Chrome or Edge: <https://keybard.svalboard.com>

[Section titled “Video build guide”](#video-build-guide)

![](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/fa_BZ1AKQVk/hqdefault.jpg)

## What’s in the kit

[Section titled “What’s in the kit”](#whats-in-the-kit)

This is the standard packing list for Lightly FDM V2.0. It can vary a little between kit versions. We pack by weight and include a spare or two of most hardware. You can buy more of the small hardware on Amazon or AliExpress.

| Part                                                                                                                    | Minimum count                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| N35 magnets                                                                                                             | about 200 (100, plus 100 spare) |
| M3x4 heat set inserts                                                                                                   | 14 (12, plus 2 spare)           |
| M5x5.7 heat set inserts                                                                                                 | 4                               |
| 1/4-20 heat set inserts                                                                                                 | 2                               |
| Cluster PCBAs                                                                                                           | 10 (2 spare)                    |
| Thumb PCBAs                                                                                                             | 2                               |
| Main PCBAs (MCUs)                                                                                                       | 2                               |
| 150 mm FFCs (flat flexible cables)                                                                                      | 12 (10, plus 2 spare)           |
| M2 x 4 mm T6 thread-cutting screws, for PCBAs and the TrackPoint holder (and the set screws of older tripod palm rests) | 46 (44, plus 2 spare)           |
| M3 6 mm screws, for cases and clusters                                                                                  | 40 (32, plus 8 spare)           |
| M3 square nuts                                                                                                          | 32 (24, plus 8 spare)           |
| M3 6 mm thread-cutting screws, for the main PCB                                                                         | 9 (8, plus 1 spare)             |
| M5 16 mm flat head screws, for the palm rests                                                                           | 2                               |
| M5 thin square nuts, for the palm rests                                                                                 | 2                               |
| Stainless steel towers for clusters                                                                                     | set of 10                       |
| Rubber feet (FC-036-DCW-PT)                                                                                             | 9 (4 per side)                  |
| T10 Torx driver, for the M3 x 6 mm screws                                                                               | 1                               |
| T6 Torx bit, for the M2 x 4 mm screws                                                                                   | 1                               |
| 3 mm hex key, for the palm rest center screws                                                                           | 1                               |
| USB-C to USB-C cables                                                                                                   | 2                               |
| TrackPoint PCBA                                                                                                         | optional                        |
| Trackball PCBA                                                                                                          | optional                        |

The kit has twice the magnets you need, so you can build simple magnet fixtures. They make assembly much more reliable and tidy (Step 2).

### Trackballs and static bearings

[Section titled “Trackballs and static bearings”](#trackballs-and-static-bearings)

Kits don’t include a trackball or the static bearing balls. Buy them separately.

* **Static bearings:** 3.175 mm ceramic (ZrO2) balls. We recommend [G5 grade on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/uxcell-Ceramic-Bearing-Zirconium-Precision/dp/B081SNH8J5). Some older holder designs use 3 mm balls ([G5 on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/uxcell-Ceramic-Bearing-Zirconium-Precision/dp/B081SPLWT5)).

* **Trackballs:**

  * Svalboard Bright Silver, 44 mm: in the [Trackball Upgrade Kit](https://svalboard.com/products/trackball-upgrade-kit), option “Complete with Bright Silver ball - 44mm”.
  * [SANWA 44 mm red trackball](https://www.amazon.com/SANWA-Trackball-Replacement-Kensington-Compatible/dp/B0BQV1X86B)

**Trackball size:** 44 mm is the default and suits any user. Larger balls need big hands: at least 190 mm, and more likely 200 mm, from wrist to the tip of the middle finger, with a fairly arched fit. A bigger ball affects fit, so start from 44 mm.

### Handle the PCBAs safely

[Section titled “Handle the PCBAs safely”](#handle-the-pcbas-safely)

Static can damage the PCBAs.

* Every PCBA is tested and packed in static-dissipative bags or wrap. The exception is the finger cluster PCBAs. They aren’t fully tested, so the kit includes two spares. Test them before final assembly ([Step 7](/build/#step-7-install-pcbas-and-test)).
* The odds of three bad finger PCBAs are about 1 in 1,000. If that happens, contact <support@svalboard.com> for a replacement.
* Use ESD-safe handling: a properly grounded ESD mat and a wrist strap. We can’t take responsibility for PCBAs damaged during assembly.
* Take extra care in dry climates or on carpet.

## Tools you need

[Section titled “Tools you need”](#tools-you-need)

**Required:**

* A 3D printer with a 0.4 mm nozzle, or access to one (for example, at a library or makerspace). We recommend Bambu printers, but anything from a Prusa MK3S up can do the job.
* At least one full spool of filament. Black PLA is the basic choice. Any filament that isn’t opaque to infrared light at 940 nm needs [silver Sharpie](https://www.amazon.com/Sharpie-39108PP-Metallic-Permanent-Blister/dp/B00009RAX4) on the key flags ([Step 5](/build/#step-5-ink-the-key-flags)). Only Sharpie-brand silver works reliably. Sharpie gold, bronze and copper are less reliable.
* [Medium CA glue, with fine applicator tips](https://a.co/d/0MWOtlK).
* Adjustable parallel pliers. We recommend the [Knipex Pliers Wrench, 180 mm](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B081K8WFTF).
* A small flat-blade screwdriver, about 4 mm wide and 1 mm thick.
* A heat set insert kit or a soldering iron, for example [this one](https://amzn.to/3TOY4MW).
* 3D printing experience. This is an advanced build. Depending on your filament and your printer, you may need to tune your slicer settings to get working parts.

**Recommended:**

* Diamond files for cleanup (200 and 400 grit).
* A #2 X-Acto knife.

## The steps

[Section titled “The steps”](#the-steps)

1. [Print all parts and clean them up](/build/#step-1-print-all-parts)
2. [Organize magnets for assembly](/build/#step-2-organize-magnets)
3. [Install magnets in keys and clusters](/build/#step-3-install-magnets)
4. [Insert square nuts, then keys, into clusters](/build/#step-4-insert-keys)
5. [Apply paint or ink to key flags as needed](/build/#step-5-ink-the-key-flags)
6. [Attach FFCs to PCBAs](/build/#step-6-attach-ffcs)
7. [Install PCBAs in clusters, then test them (recommended)](/build/#step-7-install-pcbas-and-test)
8. [Install inserts and nuts in base and cover](/build/#step-8-install-inserts-and-nuts)
9. [Attach towers to clusters](/build/#step-9-attach-towers-to-clusters)
10. [Install towers on baseplates and clusters on towers](/build/#step-10-install-towers-on-baseplates), then the pointing devices: [10a TrackPoint, 10b trackball, 10c touchpad](/build/#steps-10a-to-10c-pointing-devices)
11. [Route cables through baseplates](/build/#step-11-route-cables)
12. [Install MCUs on baseplates and connect cables](/build/#step-12-install-mcus)
13. [Attach palm rest carriers to baseplates](/build/#step-13-attach-palm-rest-carriers)
14. [Attach palm rests to carriers](/build/#step-14-attach-palm-rests)
15. [Flash firmware and connect the cables](/build/#step-15-flash-firmware-and-connect)
16. [Test all keys in Keybard](/build/#step-16-test-all-keys)
17. [Install back cover and rubber feet](/build/#step-17-install-back-cover-and-feet)
18. [Adjust fit for both hands](/build/#step-18-adjust-the-fit)
19. [Enjoy!](/build/#step-19-enjoy)

## Sizing before you build

[Section titled “Sizing before you build”](#sizing-before-you-build)

Print your keys to fit your fingertips. Measure first, then print ([Step 1](/build/#step-1-print-all-parts)).

### Choose your key width

[Section titled “Choose your key width”](#choose-your-key-width)

Svalboard is most comfortable with the keys as close to your fingers as possible, without being so close that you press keys by accident.

1. Print the fingertip sizer at 100%, with no scaling: [svalboard.com/sizer](http://svalboard.com/sizer).
2. Place each fingertip in the crescents. Find the smallest crescent where your fingertip width at the bottom line is the same as the line, or slightly smaller.
3. Write down the width for each finger in the table on the sizer.
4. Pick the key size that fits your **largest** fingertip.

The sizer measures fingertip width 6 mm from the tip. That is the depth of a finger cluster, from the center key surface to the edge of the side keys.

![The Svalboard fingertip sizer: crescents from 14 mm to 20 mm wide, a fingertip drawn in the 14 mm crescent, and a table to record the width of each finger.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/fitment-sizer.CxHaFAfJ_ZCHX1f.webp)

### Key sizes

[Section titled “Key sizes”](#key-sizes)

There are four side key sizes. In order of increasing fingertip space:

| Size         | Approximate spacing |
| ------------ | ------------------- |
| Thick (+1)   | 16 mm               |
| Semi (+0.5)  | 17 mm               |
| Thin (0)     | 18 mm               |
| Backset (−1) | 20 mm               |

* People with thin or pointed fingertips may prefer the thicker keys.
* People with blunt or wide fingertips may need the Backset keys for enough room to type comfortably.
* North keys come in Thick (+1) only.

The spacing is roughly the space between opposite side keys, near their tops. The numbers are approximate: use them to compare sizes, not as exact measurements.

![The four side key sizes cut through the middle, side by side: Thick (+1) about 16 mm, Semi (+0.5) about 17 mm, Thin (0) about 18 mm and Backset (−1) about 20 mm. A dashed line runs along the front face of each key base. A solid line touches the bottom front edge of each key top, with a short bracket to the dashed line. On Backset, a thin dashed curve extends the key top's front face down past its lead-in ramp to that same bottom edge. The key top sits forward of the base by +1.0 mm on Thick and +0.5 mm on Semi, in line with it on Thin, and 1.0 mm behind it on Backset.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-profiles-line-light.BLMaTeuA_1PzfFg.webp)![The four side key sizes cut through the middle, side by side: Thick (+1) about 16 mm, Semi (+0.5) about 17 mm, Thin (0) about 18 mm and Backset (−1) about 20 mm. A dashed line runs along the front face of each key base. A solid line touches the bottom front edge of each key top, with a short bracket to the dashed line. On Backset, a thin dashed curve extends the key top's front face down past its lead-in ramp to that same bottom edge. The key top sits forward of the base by +1.0 mm on Thick and +0.5 mm on Semi, in line with it on Thin, and 1.0 mm behind it on Backset.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-profiles-line-dark.CCsglw0P_scPIA.webp)![The four side key sizes cut through the middle, side by side: Thick (+1) about 16 mm, Semi (+0.5) about 17 mm, Thin (0) about 18 mm and Backset (−1) about 20 mm. A dashed line runs along the front face of each key base. A solid line touches the bottom front edge of each key top, with a short bracket to the dashed line. On Backset, a thin dashed curve extends the key top's front face down past its lead-in ramp to that same bottom edge. The key top sits forward of the base by +1.0 mm on Thick and +0.5 mm on Semi, in line with it on Thin, and 1.0 mm behind it on Backset.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-profiles-shaded-light.BX2UhJkA_ZkBExC.webp)![The four side key sizes cut through the middle, side by side: Thick (+1) about 16 mm, Semi (+0.5) about 17 mm, Thin (0) about 18 mm and Backset (−1) about 20 mm. A dashed line runs along the front face of each key base. A solid line touches the bottom front edge of each key top, with a short bracket to the dashed line. On Backset, a thin dashed curve extends the key top's front face down past its lead-in ramp to that same bottom edge. The key top sits forward of the base by +1.0 mm on Thick and +0.5 mm on Semi, in line with it on Thin, and 1.0 mm behind it on Backset.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-profiles-shaded-dark.oMrJcEPA_Z1tRcgb.webp)

The four side key sizes, cut through the middle. The dashed line is the front of the key base; the solid line is the bottom front edge of the key top. On Backset, the key top's front face is extended down past the lead-in ramp. The numbers are how far the key top sits forward of the base, in mm: + is forward, − is back.

![Four finger clusters cut through the middle, one for each side key size, with a dimension line between the East and West keys: Thick (+1) about 16 mm, Semi (+0.5) about 17 mm, Thin (0) about 18 mm, Backset (−1) about 20 mm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-sizing-line-light.BfWJIKyu_14HKnL.webp)![Four finger clusters cut through the middle, one for each side key size, with a dimension line between the East and West keys: Thick (+1) about 16 mm, Semi (+0.5) about 17 mm, Thin (0) about 18 mm, Backset (−1) about 20 mm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-sizing-line-dark.BDvrYmwP_MQO5z.webp)![Four finger clusters cut through the middle, one for each side key size, with a dimension line between the East and West keys: Thick (+1) about 16 mm, Semi (+0.5) about 17 mm, Thin (0) about 18 mm, Backset (−1) about 20 mm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-sizing-shaded-light.DJFqg6Rj_1Cb1U5.webp)![Four finger clusters cut through the middle, one for each side key size, with a dimension line between the East and West keys: Thick (+1) about 16 mm, Semi (+0.5) about 17 mm, Thin (0) about 18 mm, Backset (−1) about 20 mm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-sizing-shaded-dark.D7nPMC0x_ZRQiHn.webp)

Approximate space between opposite side keys for each key size.

### Other hand measurements

[Section titled “Other hand measurements”](#other-hand-measurements)

Only fingertip width calls for different parts. Every Svalboard has plenty of adjustment range for the rest. Hand size can help you pick a trackball size:

* **Hand length**, wrist to the tip of the middle finger: under 170 mm is extra small, 170 mm small, 180 mm medium, 190 mm large, over 195 mm extra large.
* **Palm width** at the knuckles: under 75 mm is small, 75 to 85 mm medium, over 85 mm large.

44 mm is the default trackball size. See [Trackballs and static bearings](/build/#trackballs-and-static-bearings).

![An example hand with its measurements: whole hand 180 mm, thumb to index 65 mm, index to middle 15 mm, middle to ring -9 mm, ring to pinky -28 mm, palm width at the knuckles 76 mm, and last thumb knuckle 30 mm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/fitment-hand-measurements.C4tiP7Ys_Z1HYQaq.webp)

## Step 1: Print all parts

[Section titled “Step 1: Print all parts”](#step-1-print-all-parts)

### Get the files

[Section titled “Get the files”](#get-the-files)

The parts are in the [svalboard-self-print repository](https://github.com/svalboard/svalboard-self-print/). If you don’t have access yet, ask @claussen on the [Svalboard Discord](https://www.svalboard.com/discord).

### Which version to print

[Section titled “Which version to print”](#which-version-to-print)

* In general, use the latest version.
* V2.0 greatly improves the key mechanism tolerances. Use it unless you’re building to match older printed parts.
* Keys and clusters **must** come from the same major version, or they won’t fit together.
* Many other parts didn’t change from V1.3 to V2.0 and were carried forward as they are.
* The repository may hold prototypes or parts that aren’t in your kit. If you’re unsure whether a part fits, ask in #supporters on Discord.

### What to print

[Section titled “What to print”](#what-to-print)

Pick your side key size first. See [Sizing before you build](/build/#sizing-before-you-build).

**Finger keys**

* 8 North keys: 11 mm tall, Thick (+1, 16 mm), medium force (0.7 mm offset).
* 24 East, South and West side keys: 6 mm tall, in your size: Thick (+1, 16 mm), Semi (+0.5, 17 mm), Thin (0, 18 mm) or Backset (−1, 20 mm). Medium force (0.7 mm offset).
* 8 tipping center keys: 0.9 mm offset is a good starting point.

**Thumb keys**

* 2 Pad, 2 Knuckle, 2 Down, Nail Left and Nail Right.
* 2 Up keys: Mode Slim 29h. Print the “Mode (Up) 29h” key from `Thumb Side Keys All v2.0 RCe.step` in the `Lightly FDM/V2.0/V2.0 Keys/Thumb Side Keys` folder.

**Clusters**

* 8 finger clusters
* Thumb L and Thumb R

**Other parts**

* Palm rests: Hemi Palm L, Hemi Palm R, two 9 mm hemi carriers (“2N-Slots”), and two hemi top washers. The files are in the Hemi Palms folder under Palmrests. Carriers from 1 mm to 15 mm tall are in its “Additional carrier variants and heights” folder.

* Base plates and cases: L Base, L Case, R Base, R Case. For a compact board with no palm rest, print the [sawed-off case](/build/#sawed-off-case) instead.

* TrackPoint case, if you have a TrackPoint: top cover and bottom cover.

* Tools: mini 4x3 magnet stages (Key and Cluster), magnet dropper, mini key tray fixture.

![The printed parts for one half laid out at the same scale: finger cluster (print 4), thumb cluster, palm rest, carrier and top washer, then North key (4), side key (12), tipping center key (4), and the Nail, Knuckle, Pad, Up and Down thumb keys.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-parts-one-half-line-light.CgltFQTB_Z17il5n.webp)![The printed parts for one half laid out at the same scale: finger cluster (print 4), thumb cluster, palm rest, carrier and top washer, then North key (4), side key (12), tipping center key (4), and the Nail, Knuckle, Pad, Up and Down thumb keys.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-parts-one-half-line-dark.CJfcnIWJ_Z21Y86f.webp)![The printed parts for one half laid out at the same scale: finger cluster (print 4), thumb cluster, palm rest, carrier and top washer, then North key (4), side key (12), tipping center key (4), and the Nail, Knuckle, Pad, Up and Down thumb keys.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-parts-one-half-shaded-light.BHnCIszZ_Z1hMr2r.webp)![The printed parts for one half laid out at the same scale: finger cluster (print 4), thumb cluster, palm rest, carrier and top washer, then North key (4), side key (12), tipping center key (4), and the Nail, Knuckle, Pad, Up and Down thumb keys.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-parts-one-half-shaded-dark.Ca8EOUlI_Za66H0.webp)

The printed parts for one half (right half shown). Base plate and case not shown.

### Print tuning

[Section titled “Print tuning”](#print-tuning)

* Use a smooth or satin build plate. Fully textured plates make the parts look rough. This is only about looks. We recommend the Fabreeko HoneyBadger SemiSatin plate.
* Only the palm rests and the tipping center keys need supports.
* Start by getting the 6 mm side key perfect, then the finger and thumb clusters. If you can print those, the rest is easy.

### Keys

[Section titled “Keys”](#keys)

* PLA: 0.12 mm layer height, 0.18 mm first layer.
* ABS: the same settings work, but the filament must be very dry. ABS is finicky with overhangs if it’s even a little damp.
* Exterior perimeters: 0.3 mm.
* You may need to paint seam blockers on the sides of the small flag on each key.

![Slicer view of a full build plate with two sets of keys, all except the thumb Down keys.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/print-key-plate.Bk522esP_Z1BCRLg.webp)

#### Key flags

[Section titled “Key flags”](#key-flags)

The flag is the thin tab under each key that blocks the optical sensor.

* If flags form badly, place the seams at the top corner of the flag. Seams on the flag face can leave pinholes and heat artifacts that let light through.
* The flags must be about 0.8 mm thick or less for the parts to fit. With a 0.4 mm nozzle, set exterior perimeters (“outer wall” in Orca and Bambu Studio) to 0.3 mm.
* You may still need to clean up stringing. Slower printers and wet filament make stringing worse.
* If your filament isn’t opaque to infrared light, coat the flags with opaque marker. Silver Sharpie works well ([Step 5](/build/#step-5-ink-the-key-flags)).

![A 6 mm side key lying flat as it prints, with the key top, stem, magnet pocket and flag labeled. A ring marks the top corner of the flag, where the seams should go.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-flag-line-light.B5yeOLkz_2Oma6.webp)![A 6 mm side key lying flat as it prints, with the key top, stem, magnet pocket and flag labeled. A ring marks the top corner of the flag, where the seams should go.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-flag-line-dark.CNmZ6_md_Zh8xq3.webp)![A 6 mm side key lying flat as it prints, with the key top, stem, magnet pocket and flag labeled. A ring marks the top corner of the flag, where the seams should go.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-flag-shaded-light.BIZx65w5_ZhYVlP.webp)![A 6 mm side key lying flat as it prints, with the key top, stem, magnet pocket and flag labeled. A ring marks the top corner of the flag, where the seams should go.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-flag-shaded-dark.l5jPFhue_ZQHQKC.webp)

Put the seams at the top corner of the flag.

#### Key force

[Section titled “Key force”](#key-force)

The offset sets how hard a key is to press. A larger offset gives a lighter key.

#### Tipping center keys

[Section titled “Tipping center keys”](#tipping-center-keys)

The tipping center key is the standard center key. The default strength is 0.9 mm offset, about 20 g. The STEP file has every offset from 0 to 1.2 mm (very light) if you want to experiment.

* Print at 0.2 mm layer height.
* Make the supports very dense: 0 or 0.1 mm base pattern spacing, and zero interface layer spacing (a very dense support interface).
* Dense supports come off as one block and leave a clean surface, so you have little or no cleanup inside the light hole.

![Slicer support settings with the base pattern spacing set to 0.1 mm, next to a tipping center key on dense green supports.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/print-tipping-center-key-supports.wPCXYSOB_SGTtt.webp)

### Clusters

[Section titled “Clusters”](#clusters)

* 0.2 mm layer height.
* Arachne on is recommended.
* The tipping center key clusters don’t need supports.
* Bridging angle 0 (automatic).[\*](#older-b-bridging)
* If your printer can print two colors, print the small diffusers for the RGB layer lights in white.

![Slicer view of the cluster plate. Yellow bridging modifiers on the clusters are set to 90°, 157.2°, 166.2°, 193.8° and 202.8°.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/print-cluster-plate.BA-PuCiX_1PcjA1.webp)

In the slicer preview, check that the first layer over each key well bridges the short way across it. The dashed outlines mark the openings.

![Slicer view of a finger cluster at the first bridge layer over its key wells. Blue bridge lines fill each of the four wells, running across the narrow dimension of each dashed opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/print-cluster-bridges.C7Xgwqhu_28cY50.webp)

![Close-up of one finger cluster key well at the first bridge layer, from the top and from below. The blue bridge lines cross the narrow dashed opening. An arrow marks that bridges run the short way.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/print-cluster-bridge-finger-well.BbgWVdzu_277Dkx.webp)

![Close-up of one thumb cluster key well at the first bridge layer, from the top and from below. The blue bridge lines cross the narrow dashed opening. An arrow marks that bridges run the short way.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/print-cluster-bridge-thumb-well.eDZO3z2Q_Z2su2wO.webp)

#### Thumb Down key opening

[Section titled “Thumb Down key opening”](#thumb-down-key-opening)

The marked edge of the thumb cluster **must** be square. Elephant’s foot here makes the thumb Down key bind. A bevel here can add play to the key and change how it feels.

![A right thumb cluster seen from below. A heavy orange line marks the edge of the Down key opening that must stay square.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-down-edge-line-light.DQcsSzvq_Z1fvqKl.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen from below. A heavy orange line marks the edge of the Down key opening that must stay square.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-down-edge-line-dark.ZNgBP7Lr_1vNIkY.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen from below. A heavy orange line marks the edge of the Down key opening that must stay square.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-down-edge-shaded-light.ClNBD1mA_2eCyua.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen from below. A heavy orange line marks the edge of the Down key opening that must stay square.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-down-edge-shaded-dark.CGNuGUy-_Z1xR8tv.webp)

Keep this edge of the Down key opening square: no elephant's foot, no bevel.

### Cases and base plates

[Section titled “Cases and base plates”](#cases-and-base-plates)

* 0.2 mm layer height, 6 walls.
* Smooth side down.
* No supports.
* **External bridge infill direction** 0 (automatic), for cases and base plates.

The base plates also need one modifier each:

1. On each plate, add a box modifier over the index finger tower slot: the finger tower slot closest to the thumb slots. Make the box cover the whole slot without reaching the next finger tower slot.
2. In the modifier’s settings, set **External bridge infill direction** to 94° on the left plate and 86° on the right plate.

![Slicer views of the left and right base plates at the first bridge layer over the slots. On each plate, a yellow box marks the one modifier over the index finger tower slot: 94° on the left plate, 86° on the right. Every other slot bridges automatically.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/print-baseplate-bridges.BZEbkzPg_Z24CTY8.webp)

In the slicer preview, check that the first layer over each slot bridges the short way across it. The dashed outlines mark the openings.

![Close-up of the index finger tower slot on the left plate at the first bridge layer, from the top and from below. Inside the 94° modifier box, the blue bridge lines cross the dashed opening the short way. An arrow marks that bridges run the short way.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/print-baseplate-bridge-index-slot.oede5YLn_1ufB3q.webp)

![Close-up of the two thumb slots on the left plate at the first bridge layer, from the top and from below. With automatic bridging, the blue bridge lines cross each dashed opening the short way. An arrow marks that bridges run the short way.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/print-baseplate-bridge-thumb-slot.WQSDjp7L_Zy0KNi.webp)

### Palm rests and carriers

[Section titled “Palm rests and carriers”](#palm-rests-and-carriers)

* Print every palm rest part with 6 walls for strength.
* Stand each palm rest on its flat long edge, with tree supports (Auto, Default or Organic) and a brim of 5 mm or more. You may want to paint seam blockers on the visible surfaces.
* Print the carriers and the top washers flat side down. They don’t need supports.

![A palm rest standing on its long flat edge on a build plate, with a carrier and a top washer lying flat side down beside it.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-print-orientation-line-light.DngG6ZYf_Ua459.webp)![A palm rest standing on its long flat edge on a build plate, with a carrier and a top washer lying flat side down beside it.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-print-orientation-line-dark.ugocG4aL_cktky.webp)![A palm rest standing on its long flat edge on a build plate, with a carrier and a top washer lying flat side down beside it.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-print-orientation-shaded-light.Br39J5dG_UTXM0.webp)![A palm rest standing on its long flat edge on a build plate, with a carrier and a top washer lying flat side down beside it.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-print-orientation-shaded-dark.D3rvWeRZ_1o03nK.webp)

Print orientation for the palm rest parts. Supports and brim are not shown.

![The parts of a hemispherical palm rest, pulled apart from top to bottom: the M5 flat head screw (orange), the hemispherical top washer, the palm rest with the ball on its underside, the carrier with its cup, and the M5 square nut (orange).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-exploded-line-light.DaEOOYj6_Z2ffYv4.webp)![The parts of a hemispherical palm rest, pulled apart from top to bottom: the M5 flat head screw (orange), the hemispherical top washer, the palm rest with the ball on its underside, the carrier with its cup, and the M5 square nut (orange).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-exploded-line-dark.zlyEoOor_2hPO4x.webp)![The parts of a hemispherical palm rest, pulled apart from top to bottom: the M5 flat head screw (orange), the hemispherical top washer, the palm rest with the ball on its underside, the carrier with its cup, and the M5 square nut (orange).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-exploded-shaded-light.Dxj0U0ys_2va3UY.webp)![The parts of a hemispherical palm rest, pulled apart from top to bottom: the M5 flat head screw (orange), the hemispherical top washer, the palm rest with the ball on its underside, the carrier with its cup, and the M5 square nut (orange).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-exploded-shaded-dark.BdM27Y2Q_sTtdq.webp)

#### Older builds: tripod palm rests

[Section titled “Older builds: tripod palm rests”](#older-builds-tripod-palm-rests)

Print the tripod palm rests the same way, standing on the long edge with tree supports and a brim. Print the carriers and shims without supports.

![Slicer view of a tripod palm rest standing on its long edge with tree supports, next to two carriers and a set of shims.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/print-palm-rests.2DpxzzM5_1Uig9U.webp)

### Sawed-off case

[Section titled “Sawed-off case”](#sawed-off-case)

The sawed-off case shortens each unit: base plate and back case end just behind the cluster slots, with no palm rest. It packs small for travel, and it’s the one to choose if you bring your own palm rest setup.

Print the sawed-off base plates and cases from the [Sawed-off Case folder](https://github.com/svalboard/svalboard-self-print/tree/main/Lightly%20FDM/V2.0/Baseplates%20and%20Case/Sawed-off%20Case) in place of the standard ones. Its one STEP file holds both halves. Print them the same way as the [standard cases and base plates](/build/#cases-and-base-plates). Skip the palm rest parts, and skip [Steps 13 and 14](/build/#step-13-attach-palm-rest-carriers).

The sawed-off base plates have five case screw holes. Check the back of yours the same way as the standard plates ([Which base plates you have](/build/#which-base-plates-you-have)), then fit five square nuts or five heat set inserts per plate to match.

![Two right halves at the same scale, each a base plate on its back case. The standard one on the left runs long behind the cluster slots, with the palm rest slot. The sawed-off one on the right ends just behind the cluster slots and has no palm rest slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-sawed-off-case-line-light.wRitwZ6N_ZNxUg1.webp)![Two right halves at the same scale, each a base plate on its back case. The sawed-off one on the right ends just behind the cluster slots and has no palm rest slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-sawed-off-case-line-dark.B74WLxcR_Z1NSofi.webp)![Two right halves at the same scale, each a base plate on its back case. The standard one on the left runs long behind the cluster slots, with the palm rest slot. The sawed-off one on the right ends just behind the cluster slots and has no palm rest slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-sawed-off-case-shaded-light.DJ0JXRM6_1ySI4P.webp)![Two right halves at the same scale, each a base plate on its back case. The standard one on the left runs long behind the cluster slots, with the palm rest slot. The sawed-off one on the right ends just behind the cluster slots and has no palm rest slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-sawed-off-case-shaded-dark.DwA30Xoc_14iqXk.webp)

The standard right base plate and case beside the sawed-off one, at the same scale.

* 0.2 mm layer height.

### Deprecated parts

Don’t print the center key sliders (gap sliders) or the printed towers. The tipping center keys and clusters replace the sliders, and the kit includes stainless steel towers.

Older builds

1. \* V1.3 and earlier clusters use bridging angle 180°, plus bridging modifiers at the angles in the slicer view. [↩︎](#older-ref-b-bridging)

## Step 2: Organize magnets

[Section titled “Step 2: Organize magnets”](#step-2-organize-magnets)

Organize the magnets by polarity before you glue them in. Every magnet must face the right way:

* **Keys:** the **south** pole faces out of the key.
* **Clusters:** the **north** pole faces out of the cluster.

![A cut-away close-up of an East key in its cluster. The key magnet sits in the key with its south pole facing the cluster wall; the cluster magnet sits in the wall with its north pole facing the key. Orange halves are north, blue halves are south.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnet-polarity-line-light.BRWxISwM_ZPiOeH.webp)![A cut-away close-up of an East key in its cluster. The key magnet sits in the key with its south pole facing the cluster wall; the cluster magnet sits in the wall with its north pole facing the key. Orange halves are north, blue halves are south.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnet-polarity-line-dark.DJ_-Y5Dr_20dLWb.webp)![A cut-away close-up of an East key in its cluster. The key magnet sits in the key with its south pole facing the cluster wall; the cluster magnet sits in the wall with its north pole facing the key. Orange halves are north, blue halves are south.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnet-polarity-shaded-light.CPrJ0B2C_112h78.webp)![A cut-away close-up of an East key in its cluster. The key magnet sits in the key with its south pole facing the cluster wall; the cluster magnet sits in the wall with its north pole facing the key. Orange halves are north, blue halves are south.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnet-polarity-shaded-dark.t5C-SqBI_v0deW.webp)

Opposite poles face each other: south out of the key, north out of the cluster.

If you don’t have a reference to tell the poles apart, use a compass. Hold the magnet in your fingers or in something non-metal, so nothing else affects the reading.

There are several good ways to stage the magnets.

### Magnet stages

[Section titled “Magnet stages”](#magnet-stages)

The magnet stages hold magnets in rows on their top surface, all with the same pole up.

1. Glue magnets into the back of the stage, all with the same polarity. This turns the stage into a magnetic base.
2. On the **Key** magnet stage, the working surface must hold magnets with the **south** pole up.
3. On the **Cluster** magnet stage, the working surface must hold magnets with the **north** pole up.
4. Drop as many magnets as you need onto the stage.
5. Pick them up one at a time with a small flat screwdriver, and press each into a key or cluster. They always come off the stage with the right pole out.

For a single build, print the compact 4x3 stages, or fill one row or column of the larger 8x8 stage.

![The compact 4x3 Key and Cluster magnet stages side by side, each with 12 magnets on its top face. The Key stage holds magnets south pole up, the Cluster stage north pole up.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnet-stages-line-light.ogVwROs0_Z3e8IL.webp)![The compact 4x3 Key and Cluster magnet stages side by side, each with 12 magnets on its top face. The Key stage holds magnets south pole up, the Cluster stage north pole up.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnet-stages-line-dark.BFi-x3jo_Z5svNS.webp)![The compact 4x3 Key and Cluster magnet stages side by side, each with 12 magnets on its top face. The Key stage holds magnets south pole up, the Cluster stage north pole up.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnet-stages-shaded-light.DOEwsyEk_2ialE4.webp)![The compact 4x3 Key and Cluster magnet stages side by side, each with 12 magnets on its top face. The Key stage holds magnets south pole up, the Cluster stage north pole up.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnet-stages-shaded-dark.CJ6aJ4yV_27v7Ko.webp)

The compact 4x3 magnet stages. The Key stage holds magnets south pole up; the Cluster stage, north pole up.

### Magnet dispenser

[Section titled “Magnet dispenser”](#magnet-dispenser)

The magnet dispenser holds a stack of magnets and drops them one at a time onto a stage. Print it at 0.3 mm layer height with no supports.

![The magnet dispenser in a slicer, as a 3D model, and printed, held in a hand.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/magnet-dispenser.021uxXI__Z1IAYWX.webp)

### Alternative: a MagSafe phone

[Section titled “Alternative: a MagSafe phone”](#alternative-a-magsafe-phone)

You can also stage magnet stacks on the MagSafe ring of an iPhone 12 or newer. This works even with a MagSafe case on.

* The stack farther from the center has the **south** pole up. Use it for keys.
* The stack closer to the center has the **north** pole up. Use it for clusters.

Reference: page 152 of Apple’s *Accessory Design Guidelines for Apple Devices*.

To install a magnet, pick one up from the correct stack with a magnetic tool, put a drop of glue in the magnet hole, and insert the magnet.

## Step 3: Install magnets

[Section titled “Step 3: Install magnets”](#step-3-install-magnets)

Each finger cluster has 5 keys, so a finished cluster with its keys needs 10 magnets.

All magnets are 2.0 mm x 1.5 mm N35.

* **Clusters:** the **north** pole faces out.
* **Keys:** the **south** pole faces out, so it’s the visible side.

### Install key magnets: dip method

[Section titled “Install key magnets: dip method”](#install-key-magnets-dip-method)

1. Use the Key stage (south pole up).
2. Put magnets on the stage.
3. Put a small blob of CA glue on a surface. A strip of painter’s tape works well.
4. Pick up a magnet with a thin flat-blade screwdriver.
5. Dip the magnet in the glue.
6. Press it into the hole in the key.
7. Squeeze the magnet flush with parallel pliers.
8. Let the glue cure before you use the key.

![Two cut-away views of a key with its magnet. Before: the magnet stands proud of the key between the open jaws of parallel pliers. After: the jaws are closed and the magnet is flush.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnet-flush-line-light.CkaEtmJh_ZvFwaB.webp)![Two cut-away views of a key with its magnet. Before: the magnet stands proud of the key between the open jaws of parallel pliers. After: the jaws are closed and the magnet is flush.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnet-flush-line-dark.CeqU93Wj_29UNnM.webp)![Two cut-away views of a key with its magnet. Before: the magnet stands proud of the key between the open jaws of parallel pliers. After: the jaws are closed and the magnet is flush.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnet-flush-shaded-light.B56PxMo0_2rQBm6.webp)![Two cut-away views of a key with its magnet. Before: the magnet stands proud of the key between the open jaws of parallel pliers. After: the jaws are closed and the magnet is flush.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnet-flush-shaded-dark.4ztglOfr_1UV4VI.webp)

Squeeze the magnet flush with parallel pliers.

### Install key magnets: pre-applied glue method

[Section titled “Install key magnets: pre-applied glue method”](#install-key-magnets-pre-applied-glue-method)

1. Use the Key stage (south pole up).
2. Put magnets on the stage.
3. Put glue in the magnet holes of the keys.
4. Pick up a magnet with a thin flat-blade screwdriver.
5. Press it into the hole in the key.
6. Squeeze the magnet flush with parallel pliers.
7. Let the glue cure.

### Cluster magnets

[Section titled “Cluster magnets”](#cluster-magnets)

Install the cluster magnets the same way, from the Cluster stage (north pole up). Orange rings mark each magnet.

![A finger cluster from above and the same cluster turned over. Orange rings mark the five magnets: one in the wall of each side key slot, and the center key magnet on the underside.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnets-finger-cluster-line-light.CbBnbjrf_U54x1.webp)![A finger cluster from above and the same cluster turned over. Orange rings mark the five magnets: one in the wall of each side key slot, and the center key magnet on the underside.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnets-finger-cluster-line-dark.DdUdXhI7_Z8u8qt.webp)![A finger cluster from above and the same cluster turned over. Orange rings mark the five magnets: one in the wall of each side key slot, and the center key magnet on the underside.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnets-finger-cluster-shaded-light.COtdyp_y_1UYz1d.webp)![A finger cluster from above and the same cluster turned over. Orange rings mark the five magnets: one in the wall of each side key slot, and the center key magnet on the underside.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnets-finger-cluster-shaded-dark.Bm3ZZ7Ip_Z10QXiX.webp)

Finger cluster magnets: one in each side key slot, one for the center key on the underside.

![A right thumb cluster from above. Orange rings mark the five magnets: Nail, Knuckle, Pad, Up and Down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnets-thumb-cluster-line-light.Cu7wwzXI_13tI4y.webp)![A right thumb cluster from above. Orange rings mark the five magnets: Nail, Knuckle, Pad, Up and Down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnets-thumb-cluster-line-dark.D43EmHwA_Zx7Sok.webp)![A right thumb cluster from above. Orange rings mark the five magnets: Nail, Knuckle, Pad, Up and Down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnets-thumb-cluster-shaded-light.Bm7ISYCW_12dABs.webp)![A right thumb cluster from above. Orange rings mark the five magnets: Nail, Knuckle, Pad, Up and Down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnets-thumb-cluster-shaded-dark.CY37HPcH_2nxb3t.webp)

Thumb cluster magnets (right cluster shown; the left cluster is the mirror image).

### Key magnets

[Section titled “Key magnets”](#key-magnets)

![The keys in a row, each with its magnet in orange and ringed: North, side, tipping center, Nail, Knuckle, Pad, Up, the curved Up, and Down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnets-keys-line-light.B3Kqva3O_2mLk81.webp)![The keys in a row, each with its magnet in orange and ringed: North, side, tipping center, Nail, Knuckle, Pad, Up, the curved Up, and Down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnets-keys-line-dark.CBOF05WX_Z1v9VEG.webp)![The keys in a row, each with its magnet in orange and ringed: North, side, tipping center, Nail, Knuckle, Pad, Up, the curved Up, and Down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnets-keys-shaded-light.DBjpPaDU_ZrX09.webp)![The keys in a row, each with its magnet in orange and ringed: North, side, tipping center, Nail, Knuckle, Pad, Up, the curved Up, and Down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-magnets-keys-shaded-dark.BHXvD9Cy_2jURcI.webp)

Where the magnet goes in each key. The south pole faces out.

### Tipping center key

[Section titled “Tipping center key”](#tipping-center-key)

The tipping center key uses normal key polarity: the **south** pole faces out (up). Make sure the hole in the key is clear of stringing and stray filament.

![A tipping center key. Rings mark the magnet hole on the arm and the light hole through the stem, which must be clear of stringing.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-key-holes-line-light.D3DOSJin_ZkYV8H.webp)![A tipping center key. Rings mark the magnet hole on the arm and the light hole through the stem, which must be clear of stringing.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-key-holes-line-dark.D4ZPK9cS_eiY9D.webp)![A tipping center key. Rings mark the magnet hole on the arm and the light hole through the stem, which must be clear of stringing.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-key-holes-shaded-light.CCw0Z66g_Z1zo1Q2.webp)![A tipping center key. Rings mark the magnet hole on the arm and the light hole through the stem, which must be clear of stringing.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-key-holes-shaded-dark.CqcybpCV_Z1WJ9vg.webp)

Keep the light hole clear of stringing.

## Step 4: Insert keys

[Section titled “Step 4: Insert keys”](#step-4-insert-keys)

### Square nut first

[Section titled “Square nut first”](#square-nut-first)

Each cluster takes a square nut in the back of its underside, the fixing point for the tower. Put it in **before** you install the center key: the center key covers the nut’s slot.

1. Place the cluster top side down.
2. Line up the nut with small pliers or tweezers.
3. Press it **straight** down into the slot.

![A finger cluster upside down with no keys in it. A square nut (orange) hovers above its slot at the back, and an arrow shows it pressed straight down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-cluster-nut-line-light.YZBsehuO_Zk8uPO.webp)![A finger cluster upside down with no keys in it. A square nut (orange) hovers above its slot at the back, and an arrow shows it pressed straight down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-cluster-nut-line-dark.DQBvOdP-_Z2vJcMN.webp)![A finger cluster upside down with no keys in it. A square nut (orange) hovers above its slot at the back, and an arrow shows it pressed straight down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-cluster-nut-shaded-light.CKN8H-Pe_1PleuC.webp)![A finger cluster upside down with no keys in it. A square nut (orange) hovers above its slot at the back, and an arrow shows it pressed straight down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-cluster-nut-shaded-dark.DWrkDpg9_Z1amNwP.webp)

Before the center key goes in, press the square nut straight down into the slot at the back of the cluster.

![The same cluster, still without keys, with the square nut seated in its slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-cluster-nut-seated-line-light.Bkhnl7h1_2wqreM.webp)![The same cluster, still without keys, with the square nut seated in its slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-cluster-nut-seated-line-dark.BcVJctl0_Zt1Ccg.webp)![The same cluster, still without keys, with the square nut seated in its slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-cluster-nut-seated-shaded-light.DmlkaaWP_ZLECMp.webp)![The same cluster, still without keys, with the square nut seated in its slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-cluster-nut-seated-shaded-dark.Bk1Ged7y_Z2i9oOi.webp)

Seated: the nut sits fully in the slot.

### Insert the keys

[Section titled “Insert the keys”](#insert-the-keys)

Every key should slide easily into place and snap to its magnet.

![A finger cluster with its keys in place except the East key (orange), which is above its slot with an arrow pointing straight down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-insert-line-light.DT2LnUGG_SVR3z.webp)![A finger cluster with its keys in place except the East key (orange), which is above its slot with an arrow pointing straight down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-insert-line-dark.DdiTSB8n_ZBzAEP.webp)![A finger cluster with its keys in place except the East key (orange), which is above its slot with an arrow pointing straight down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-insert-shaded-light.Bv_Mjjfb_Z16J5Ab.webp)![A finger cluster with its keys in place except the East key (orange), which is above its slot with an arrow pointing straight down.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-insert-shaded-dark.CiAM3c_O_2bfQk0.webp)

Slide each key straight down into its slot until it snaps to its magnet.

If a key doesn’t slide in easily or doesn’t move freely:

1. File a little material off the sides of the key.
2. If it still binds, file the bottom (the chamfered back of the key base).
3. Try the fit again.

![A side key, stem down. The sides of the stem are orange, marked 1, and the chamfered bottom of the stem is blue, marked 2.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-file-areas-line-light.B0jdQZZW_YBolO.webp)![A side key, stem down. The sides of the stem are orange, marked 1, and the chamfered bottom of the stem is blue, marked 2.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-file-areas-line-dark.D48mgYOj_Z1jseb9.webp)![A side key, stem down. The sides of the stem are orange, marked 1, and the chamfered bottom of the stem is blue, marked 2.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-file-areas-shaded-light.fjzIInJ7_1y5UBr.webp)![A side key, stem down. The sides of the stem are orange, marked 1, and the chamfered bottom of the stem is blue, marked 2.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-file-areas-shaded-dark.Dpjck3kz_24g9dp.webp)

If a key binds, file the sides (1) first, then the chamfered bottom (2).

This is how each key sits in its cluster:

![A finger cluster with its keys labeled: North at the back, East, South, West, and the Center key in the middle, plus the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-finger-cluster-keys-line-light.BxJBo7jo_Z1jBbYr.webp)![A finger cluster with its keys labeled: North at the back, East, South, West, and the Center key in the middle, plus the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-finger-cluster-keys-line-dark.ByC0_wUl_ZN6l2v.webp)![A finger cluster with its keys labeled: North at the back, East, South, West, and the Center key in the middle, plus the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-finger-cluster-keys-shaded-light.Dr3rwVlo_Z1hcL65.webp)![A finger cluster with its keys labeled: North at the back, East, South, West, and the Center key in the middle, plus the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-finger-cluster-keys-shaded-dark.D-ibojLQ_2rm15I.webp)

![A right thumb cluster seen almost level from its outer side, keys labeled: the Nail and Knuckle keys in front, the Pad key behind, whose sloped top runs on into the Knuckle top as one line rising toward the Up key, the Up key, the Down key between them, the layer LED, and the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-line-light.DhxyIN4r_RnwvJ.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen almost level from its outer side, keys labeled: the Nail and Knuckle keys in front, the Pad key behind, whose sloped top runs on into the Knuckle top as one line rising toward the Up key, the Up key, the Down key between them, the layer LED, and the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-line-dark.DDzCwfv7_1Q8N6f.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen almost level from its outer side, keys labeled: the Nail and Knuckle keys in front, the Pad key behind, whose sloped top runs on into the Knuckle top as one line rising toward the Up key, the Up key, the Down key between them, the layer LED, and the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-shaded-light.DRyMLY9h_27UYIk.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen almost level from its outer side, keys labeled: the Nail and Knuckle keys in front, the Pad key behind, whose sloped top runs on into the Knuckle top as one line rising toward the Up key, the Up key, the Down key between them, the layer LED, and the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-shaded-dark.Drw6YBLA_1vTUn.webp)

![A right thumb cluster seen from the side, square to the Up slot, with the curved Up key in profile: its stem bows outward and its top curves back over the cluster. The Nail, Knuckle, Pad and Down keys are also labeled.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-curved-up-line-light.y6kgcvop_Z12Fj7T.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen from the side, square to the Up slot, with the curved Up key in profile: its stem bows outward and its top curves back over the cluster. The Nail, Knuckle, Pad and Down keys are also labeled.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-curved-up-shaded-dark.DCiJZRe7_Z25nFFT.webp)

The curved Up key, in the same cluster.

### Tipping center keys

[Section titled “Tipping center keys”](#tipping-center-keys-1)

1. Remove the North key.
2. Point the tip of the tipping center key’s arm down into the center hole of the cluster.
3. Turn the key down so the arm follows its curve through the hole, until it snaps into place.
4. Put the North key back.

![Four cut-away steps: 1, the North key lifted out of the cluster; 2, the tipping center key tilted back with the pointed tip of its arm going down into the center hole, which is ringed and labeled; 3, the key partway through its turn, with a curved arrow showing it swing down into its seat; 4, the key seated and the North key going back in.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-insert-line-light.Dk-audnI_14W9hu.webp)![Four cut-away steps: 1, the North key lifted out of the cluster; 2, the tipping center key tilted back with the pointed tip of its arm going down into the center hole, which is ringed and labeled; 3, the key partway through its turn, with a curved arrow showing it swing down into its seat; 4, the key seated and the North key going back in.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-insert-line-dark.CQ0WCSGT_n2pz3.webp)![Four cut-away steps: 1, the North key lifted out of the cluster; 2, the tipping center key tilted back with the pointed tip of its arm going down into the center hole, which is ringed and labeled; 3, the key partway through its turn, with a curved arrow showing it swing down into its seat; 4, the key seated and the North key going back in.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-insert-shaded-light.CkWcd7z3_Z1encfI.webp)![Four cut-away steps: 1, the North key lifted out of the cluster; 2, the tipping center key tilted back with the pointed tip of its arm going down into the center hole, which is ringed and labeled; 3, the key partway through its turn, with a curved arrow showing it swing down into its seat; 4, the key seated and the North key going back in.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-insert-shaded-dark.BkiChvd9_Z6TzTe.webp)

Remove North, put the arm's tip down into the center hole (ringed and labeled), turn the key down until it snaps in, then refit North.

![A finger cluster seen from underneath, with a tipping center key (orange) hooked through it. The key arm is marked 0.9.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-center-key-line-light.GFsASKCa_ZkqzgO.webp)![A finger cluster seen from underneath, with a tipping center key (orange) hooked through it. The key arm is marked 0.9.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-center-key-line-dark.C5dENizo_2b8U0w.webp)![A finger cluster seen from underneath, with a tipping center key (orange) hooked through it. The key arm is marked 0.9.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-center-key-shaded-light.wbpE32rP_Zu6V9.webp)![A finger cluster seen from underneath, with a tipping center key (orange) hooked through it. The key arm is marked 0.9.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-center-key-shaded-dark.DCCBchBz_172etB.webp)

The tipping center key replaces the older slider-based center key. Slider parts are deprecated.

## Step 5: Ink the key flags

[Section titled “Step 5: Ink the key flags”](#step-5-ink-the-key-flags)

Each key has a flag that blocks an optical sensor when you press the key. If your filament isn’t opaque to infrared light, the flags won’t block the sensors properly. Paint or ink them to make them opaque.

* We recommend [silver metallic Sharpie](https://www.amazon.com/Sharpie-39108PP-Metallic-Permanent-Blister/dp/B00009RAX4).
* Only Sharpie-brand silver works reliably.
* Very light filaments may need several coats.

Black PLA usually doesn’t need ink.

![Keys printed in light yellow and orange filament, with the flags coated in silver marker.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/key-flags-silver-marker.Bg4K3PZy_Z2nbTrc.webp)

## Step 6: Attach FFCs

[Section titled “Step 6: Attach FFCs”](#step-6-attach-ffcs)

Every FFC connects the same way:

![An FFC connector on a circuit board with its black latch standing upright over the back half of the connector. A curved arrow shows the latch's back edge lifting up and over toward the cable opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-1-open-line-light.B24TGqrv_1divjF.webp)![An FFC connector on a circuit board with its black latch standing upright over the back half of the connector. A curved arrow shows the latch's back edge lifting up and over toward the cable opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-1-open-line-dark.BIZoyHx8_Zl6DOA.webp)![An FFC connector on a circuit board with its black latch standing upright over the back half of the connector. A curved arrow shows the latch's back edge lifting up and over toward the cable opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-1-open-shaded-light.PKsDO4k7_ZJQE9z.webp)![An FFC connector on a circuit board with its black latch standing upright over the back half of the connector. A curved arrow shows the latch's back edge lifting up and over toward the cable opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-1-open-shaded-dark.ZbmAT6gW_ZKo3sF.webp)

1\. Flip the latch up.

![An FFC end being slid into the front opening of the open connector, blue stiffener on top and the contacts on the underside, facing down. An arrow shows the direction.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-2-insert-line-light.DREbXUgt_ZJQjUT.webp)![An FFC end being slid into the front opening of the open connector, blue stiffener on top and the contacts on the underside, facing down. An arrow shows the direction.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-2-insert-line-dark.DSKI7bi5_Z1dKmEI.webp)![An FFC end being slid into the front opening of the open connector, blue stiffener on top and the contacts on the underside, facing down. An arrow shows the direction.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-2-insert-shaded-light.P0KEbVBU_Z1nJeVY.webp)![An FFC end being slid into the front opening of the open connector, blue stiffener on top and the contacts on the underside, facing down. An arrow shows the direction.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-2-insert-shaded-dark.C83yLqWA_ZqQd9X.webp)

2\. Slide the cable all the way in, contacts down and blue stiffener up.

![The cable fully inserted and the latch flipped down flat at the back of the connector. A curved arrow shows the latch closing.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-3-latch-line-light.ByQ_zfCK_12MJJM.webp)![The cable fully inserted and the latch flipped down flat at the back of the connector. A curved arrow shows the latch closing.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-3-latch-line-dark.BvhJjqFr_Z3eF0n.webp)![The cable fully inserted and the latch flipped down flat at the back of the connector. A curved arrow shows the latch closing.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-3-latch-shaded-light.DDh3ZPzn_Z23J7Bu.webp)![The cable fully inserted and the latch flipped down flat at the back of the connector. A curved arrow shows the latch closing.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-3-latch-shaded-dark.CQ9HMNjb_1zwkH.webp)

3\. Flip the latch down to lock the cable.

To remove a cable, flip the latch up and pull the cable straight out.

![An MCU’s FFC connectors up close. One latch is down (closed) and one is up (open).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/ffc-latch-up-down.DWZdK56j_1RFUEr.webp)

### Attach FFCs to the PCBAs

[Section titled “Attach FFCs to the PCBAs”](#attach-ffcs-to-the-pcbas)

That orientation holds at both ends of every FFC, with one exception: at the TrackPoint PCBA the contacts face up ([Step 10a](/build/#10a-trackpoint)).

For the thumbs, use the 10-pin FFC if you have it; the RGB layer lights need it. On a thumb PCBA the latch sits on the side opposite the cable, so route the cable down through the slot after you close the latch.

![An FFC latched into the connector on the trackball PCBA. The black latch is closed flat at the back of the connector, the blue stiffener on the cable end faces up, and the cable runs straight out of the front of the connector, past the edge of the board. The contacts face down, toward the board.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-trackball-pcba-line-light.dN9Ym0uE_6UwuY.webp)![An FFC latched into the connector on the trackball PCBA. The black latch is closed flat at the back of the connector, the blue stiffener on the cable end faces up, and the cable runs straight out of the front of the connector, past the edge of the board. The contacts face down, toward the board.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-trackball-pcba-line-dark.D67j_iXd_Zt8UKD.webp)![An FFC latched into the connector on the trackball PCBA. The black latch is closed flat at the back of the connector, the blue stiffener on the cable end faces up, and the cable runs straight out of the front of the connector, past the edge of the board. The contacts face down, toward the board.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-trackball-pcba-shaded-light.B8Kfq_QL_Z1WlhKr.webp)![An FFC latched into the connector on the trackball PCBA. The black latch is closed flat at the back of the connector, the blue stiffener on the cable end faces up, and the cable runs straight out of the front of the connector, past the edge of the board. The contacts face down, toward the board.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ffc-trackball-pcba-shaded-dark.DGtMe17F_2g1Vtu.webp)

An FFC on the trackball PCBA: latch closed, blue stiffener up, contacts down.

### FFCs on the MCU

[Section titled “FFCs on the MCU”](#ffcs-on-the-mcu)

You connect the other end of each FFC to the MCU in [Step 12](/build/#step-12-install-mcus), the same way. The MCU’s 8-pin thumb connector is for older builds; use the 10-pin one.

![An MCU connected to a finger cluster PCBA by an FFC.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/ffc-on-mcu.BCdPr2A8_ZFUL4H.webp)

## Step 7: Install PCBAs and test

[Section titled “Step 7: Install PCBAs and test”](#step-7-install-pcbas-and-test)

### Install the PCBAs

[Section titled “Install the PCBAs”](#install-the-pcbas)

* Line each PCBA up squarely with the cluster before you press it in. Installing it at an angle can damage the optical sensors.
* **Finger clusters:** use just the two screws shown. If one strips, use one of the other two holes.
* Make sure the bottom-left corner of the PCBA is fully seated in the cluster. If it isn’t, the East or South key may not register.
* **Thumb clusters:** put a screw in every hole.
* You don’t need to remove the finger center key to replace a PCBA.

Use the M2 x 4 mm T6 thread-cutting screws and the T6 bit.

![A finger cluster from below with its PCBA in place. Two M2 x 4 mm T6 screws (orange) sit in opposite corners; rings mark the two spare holes and the bottom-left corner that must be fully seated.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-pcba-finger-line-light.HFy4U0kI_1RbMxG.webp)![A finger cluster from below with its PCBA in place. Two M2 x 4 mm T6 screws (orange) sit in opposite corners; rings mark the two spare holes and the bottom-left corner that must be fully seated.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-pcba-finger-line-dark.CIkJBAnB_3PgE.webp)![A finger cluster from below with its PCBA in place. Two M2 x 4 mm T6 screws (orange) sit in opposite corners; rings mark the two spare holes and the bottom-left corner that must be fully seated.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-pcba-finger-shaded-light.7nqFOUSe_1EbspO.webp)![A finger cluster from below with its PCBA in place. Two M2 x 4 mm T6 screws (orange) sit in opposite corners; rings mark the two spare holes and the bottom-left corner that must be fully seated.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-pcba-finger-shaded-dark.Bvt6azvj_2vCXdJ.webp)

Finger cluster: two M2 x 4 mm T6 screws in opposite corners. If one strips, use a spare hole. Make sure the bottom-left corner is fully seated.

![A right thumb cluster from the PCBA side with the keys removed. An M2 x 4 mm T6 screw (orange) sits in each of the six screw holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-pcba-thumb-line-light.BsXAPFvv_Z1NbEfd.webp)![A right thumb cluster from the PCBA side with the keys removed. An M2 x 4 mm T6 screw (orange) sits in each of the six screw holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-pcba-thumb-line-dark.DCGdsAXA_Og9Md.webp)![A right thumb cluster from the PCBA side with the keys removed. An M2 x 4 mm T6 screw (orange) sits in each of the six screw holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-pcba-thumb-shaded-light.7CJqzXUU_Z5mnBc.webp)![A right thumb cluster from the PCBA side with the keys removed. An M2 x 4 mm T6 screw (orange) sits in each of the six screw holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-pcba-thumb-shaded-dark.BoooJKP-_2kTvGN.webp)

Thumb cluster: an M2 x 4 mm T6 screw in every hole.

### Test the clusters (recommended)

[Section titled “Test the clusters (recommended)”](#test-the-clusters-recommended)

Test each cluster before final assembly. A bad PCBA is much easier to swap now.

Use the **blank** firmware for this test. No key does anything, so the Matrix Tester shows exactly which switches register.

1. Connect the cluster FFCs to the MCU: unlatch, insert contacts down, latch.
2. Download the blank file for that side from the vLaunch2 release: [`svalboard_left_blank_vLaunch2.uf2`](https://github.com/svalboard/qmk/releases/download/vLaunch2/svalboard_left_blank_vLaunch2.uf2) or [`svalboard_right_blank_vLaunch2.uf2`](https://github.com/svalboard/qmk/releases/download/vLaunch2/svalboard_right_blank_vLaunch2.uf2). Every file is listed in [Firmware files](/firmware/#firmware-files).
3. Flash it to the MCU. For how, see [Step 15](/build/#step-15-flash-firmware-and-connect) and [Flashing firmware](/firmware/#flashing-firmware).
4. Open [Keybard](/keybard/) (<https://keybard.svalboard.com>), choose **Connect Keyboard**, then **Matrix Tester**.
5. Press every key on the cluster. Check that each one lights up in the Matrix Tester.
6. When you’re done, disconnect the FFCs: unlatch, pull the FFC out, latch.

Flash the normal `sval` firmware in [Step 15](/build/#step-15-flash-firmware-and-connect).

## Step 8: Install inserts and nuts

[Section titled “Step 8: Install inserts and nuts”](#step-8-install-inserts-and-nuts)

The case screws hold each base plate to its back case. Depending on your base plates, those screws thread into square nuts or into heat set inserts.

### Which base plates you have

[Section titled “Which base plates you have”](#which-base-plates-you-have)

Our latest base plates use square nuts at the case screw holes. Earlier base plates, including v1.2.8, use heat set inserts, and builds of every version are out there. To check yours, turn a base plate over and look at the seven case screw holes on the back.

* If each hole has a small rectangular opening beside it, your base plates take square nuts. Follow [Square nuts at the case screw holes](#square-nuts-at-the-case-screw-holes).
* If the holes are plain and round, your base plates take heat set inserts. Follow [Heat set inserts in the base plates](#heat-set-inserts-in-the-base-plates).

The back cases take heat set inserts either way.

![Two close-ups of a case screw hole on the back of a base plate. The latest plate has a rectangular opening beside the hole; the earlier plate has a plain round hole.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-plate-identify-line-light.CltIA4Ef_1s5QMX.webp)![Two close-ups of a case screw hole on the back of a base plate. The latest plate has a rectangular opening beside the hole; the earlier plate has a plain round hole.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-plate-identify-line-dark.Bt3NWLyU_19GxSa.webp)![Two close-ups of a case screw hole on the back of a base plate. The latest plate has a rectangular opening beside the hole; the earlier plate has a plain round hole.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-plate-identify-shaded-light.D1zZ9L8w_1WFpN9.webp)![Two close-ups of a case screw hole on the back of a base plate. The latest plate has a rectangular opening beside the hole; the earlier plate has a plain round hole.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-plate-identify-shaded-dark.CTr1VCsF_11NwP4.webp)

Back of the base plate at a case screw hole. Latest plates have a square nut opening beside the hole; earlier plates have a plain round hole for a heat set insert.

### Square nuts at the case screw holes

[Section titled “Square nuts at the case screw holes”](#square-nuts-at-the-case-screw-holes)

Square nuts need no soldering iron. Each one clicks into a pocket on the back of the base plate and stays there, ready for its case screw. You need 7 M3 square nuts per base plate, DIN 562 (the thin kind: 5.5 mm across and 1.8 mm thick).

![The back of the right base plate with every square nut it holds, each seen through a small window cut in the back layer. Orange circles mark the seven case screw nuts, each over its screw hole beside a small rectangular opening. Blue circles mark the five tower slot nuts, one for each finger tower and one for the thumb tower, and the two palm rest slot nuts.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-locations-line-light.C0pzk-bd_HlDKY.webp)![The back of the right base plate with every square nut it holds, each seen through a small window cut in the back layer. Orange circles mark the seven case screw nuts, each over its screw hole beside a small rectangular opening. Blue circles mark the five tower slot nuts, one for each finger tower and one for the thumb tower, and the two palm rest slot nuts.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-locations-line-dark.DrFFAI0J_2kVPCI.webp)![The back of the right base plate with every square nut it holds, each seen through a small window cut in the back layer. Orange circles mark the seven case screw nuts, each over its screw hole beside a small rectangular opening. Blue circles mark the five tower slot nuts, one for each finger tower and one for the thumb tower, and the two palm rest slot nuts.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-locations-shaded-light.CpvBiLTV_1WtPgy.webp)![The back of the right base plate with every square nut it holds, each seen through a small window cut in the back layer. Orange circles mark the seven case screw nuts, each over its screw hole beside a small rectangular opening. Blue circles mark the five tower slot nuts, one for each finger tower and one for the thumb tower, and the two palm rest slot nuts.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-locations-shaded-dark.BxzH_Eyw_ZxrF28.webp)

All the square nuts in the right base plate: seven case screw nuts (orange), five tower slot nuts and two palm rest slot nuts (blue). Small windows in the back layer show each nut.

The left base plate is a mirror image. In the close-ups below, the thin layer of plastic over the pocket is cut away so you can see the nut.

1. Lay the base plate on the table with the back facing up.

2. Drop a nut flat into the rectangular opening beside a case screw hole.

   ![Close-up of a case screw hole from the back of the base plate. A square nut (orange) hovers above the rectangular opening, and an arrow shows it dropping in. A blue spring arm runs along each side of the opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-1-drop-line-light.Bi9MUXXq_1Q539y.webp)![Close-up of a case screw hole from the back of the base plate. A square nut (orange) hovers above the rectangular opening, and an arrow shows it dropping in. A blue spring arm runs along each side of the opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-1-drop-line-dark.DLUMUs1x_skh2h.webp)![Close-up of a case screw hole from the back of the base plate. A square nut (orange) hovers above the rectangular opening, and an arrow shows it dropping in. A blue spring arm runs along each side of the opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-1-drop-shaded-light.1PBtTqeD_ZTUAgu.webp)![Close-up of a case screw hole from the back of the base plate. A square nut (orange) hovers above the rectangular opening, and an arrow shows it dropping in. A blue spring arm runs along each side of the opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-1-drop-shaded-dark.DUZ5n_uz_Z9Fnhq.webp)

3. Push the nut sideways toward the screw hole, with a fingertip or a small screwdriver. The two spring arms bend outward to let it pass.

   ![The nut lies in the opening between the blue spring arms, and an arrow shows the push toward the screw hole.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-2-push-line-light.Bztu-htE_Z2OzL6.webp)![The nut lies in the opening between the blue spring arms, and an arrow shows the push toward the screw hole.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-2-push-line-dark.CQbIDgIo_1LcuV6.webp)![The nut lies in the opening between the blue spring arms, and an arrow shows the push toward the screw hole.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-2-push-shaded-light.DF208b5-_1nvcV6.webp)![The nut lies in the opening between the blue spring arms, and an arrow shows the push toward the screw hole.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-2-push-shaded-dark.BfZkwDV7_ZyGMX4.webp)

4. Keep pushing until the nut clicks into the pocket over the hole. The arms spring back behind it and hold it in place.

   ![The nut sits in its pocket, centered over the screw hole, with the blue arm tips behind it. A dashed line shows where the case screw goes in.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-3-seated-line-light.-RZDW8q0_Z2r43xi.webp)![The nut sits in its pocket, centered over the screw hole, with the blue arm tips behind it. A dashed line shows where the case screw goes in.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-3-seated-line-dark.BTCVUM_1_ZdbClI.webp)![The nut sits in its pocket, centered over the screw hole, with the blue arm tips behind it. A dashed line shows where the case screw goes in.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-3-seated-shaded-light.DvOpXsz2_Z153B0p.webp)![The nut sits in its pocket, centered over the screw hole, with the blue arm tips behind it. A dashed line shows where the case screw goes in.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-popnut-3-seated-shaded-dark.BtsVPRX3_1rrpG1.webp)

5. Repeat for the other six holes, then do the other base plate.

Look through each screw hole. You should see the nut’s thread centered in it.

### Heat set inserts

[Section titled “Heat set inserts”](#heat-set-inserts)

#### General process

[Section titled “General process”](#general-process)

* Set the soldering iron to about 280 °C for PLA. Lower and slower also works.
* A heat set insert tip sized for each insert is easiest. [Kits with every size are on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/Virtjoule-Heat-Insert-Tips-Sizes/dp/B08B17VQLD). A single 3 mm tip also works for all of them. It’s slower to heat the big inserts, but you don’t need to swap tips.
* A plain tapered soldering iron tip works too, but the insert is less stable and more likely to tip and foul the part.

1. Let the iron preheat for a few minutes.
2. Pick up an insert with the tip. On the base plates and cases, you can instead set the inserts in their holes and press down vertically.
3. Press the insert gently into the hole. Let the heat do the work. Forcing it can deform and ruin the part.
4. **Don’t insert it all the way.** Stop about 0.5 mm short.
5. Finish by pressing the part against a flat surface, or with a flat tool, so the insert sits flush and flat.

![A cut-away of a base plate hole with a heat set insert (orange) pressed in by the iron tip, stopped about 0.5 mm short of flush.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-heatset-1-stop-line-light.BR_tq-jz_15lHCF.webp)![A cut-away of a base plate hole with a heat set insert (orange) pressed in by the iron tip, stopped about 0.5 mm short of flush.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-heatset-1-stop-line-dark.B6zPt82t_ZUDnii.webp)![A cut-away of a base plate hole with a heat set insert (orange) pressed in by the iron tip, stopped about 0.5 mm short of flush.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-heatset-1-stop-shaded-light.9MrXn86l_KwnQu.webp)![A cut-away of a base plate hole with a heat set insert (orange) pressed in by the iron tip, stopped about 0.5 mm short of flush.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-heatset-1-stop-shaded-dark.DrPFJ1f0_24Jn5P.webp)

Stop about 0.5 mm short.

![The same cut-away with a flat tool pressing the insert down until it sits flush with the surface. An arrow shows the press.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-heatset-2-flush-line-light.B9P7r_8-_Znf25w.webp)![The same cut-away with a flat tool pressing the insert down until it sits flush with the surface. An arrow shows the press.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-heatset-2-flush-line-dark.Ct_Ypo3g_ZGcl3f.webp)![The same cut-away with a flat tool pressing the insert down until it sits flush with the surface. An arrow shows the press.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-heatset-2-flush-shaded-light.D45JomrK_1ffWbi.webp)![The same cut-away with a flat tool pressing the insert down until it sits flush with the surface. An arrow shows the press.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-heatset-2-flush-shaded-dark.BVLNT_ME_1CtIyL.webp)

Finish with a flat tool so the insert sits flush and flat.

#### Heat set inserts in the base plates

[Section titled “Heat set inserts in the base plates”](#heat-set-inserts-in-the-base-plates)

If your base plates have plain round case screw holes, install 7 M3 inserts in each base plate.

![The backs of the right and left v1.2.8 base plates. Orange rings mark the seven M3 insert holes on each.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-inserts-baseplates-line-light.BgMgNMKI_b48eB.webp)![The backs of the right and left v1.2.8 base plates. Orange rings mark the seven M3 insert holes on each.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-inserts-baseplates-line-dark.DPb-F8sz_aLgYL.webp)![The backs of the right and left v1.2.8 base plates. Orange rings mark the seven M3 insert holes on each.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-inserts-baseplates-shaded-light.Cr0PuFuz_In5dj.webp)![The backs of the right and left v1.2.8 base plates. Orange rings mark the seven M3 insert holes on each.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-inserts-baseplates-shaded-dark.Dk1hXn6g_Z2tQKuV.webp)

The seven M3 insert holes on each base plate (v1.2.8 shown, back side up).

#### Back cases

[Section titled “Back cases”](#back-cases)

Install a 1/4-20 insert in the middle of each back case, and the M5 inserts on the side. The M5 inserts are for screw-in legs.
