Back case, bottom: two M5 inserts for screw-in legs and one 1/4-20 insert in the middle.

### Square nuts in the base plate slots

[Section titled “Square nuts in the base plate slots”](#square-nuts-in-the-base-plate-slots)

The square nuts in the slots let each cluster tower bolt to the base plate anywhere along its slot.

Slot nuts go in from the front of the base plate, the side the towers mount on.

* **Latest base plates:** each slot has a nut opening on the back of the plate, with two spring arms like the case screw pockets. Drop a nut into the opening and push it along the slot past the arms.

  ![The back of the latest base plate at a slot end, with the back layer over the slot cut away. A square nut (orange) drops into the opening between two spring arms.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-latest-1-drop-line-light.B5BI9nV2_2m4ASN.webp)![The back of the latest base plate at a slot end, with the back layer over the slot cut away. A square nut (orange) drops into the opening between two spring arms.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-latest-1-drop-line-dark.B5rmYA85_1XgN17.webp)![The back of the latest base plate at a slot end, with the back layer over the slot cut away. A square nut (orange) drops into the opening between two spring arms.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-latest-1-drop-shaded-light.CgxpFVfM_2baCHw.webp)![The back of the latest base plate at a slot end, with the back layer over the slot cut away. A square nut (orange) drops into the opening between two spring arms.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-latest-1-drop-shaded-dark.BpO_Allt_2aExO7.webp)

  Latest base plates: drop a nut into the opening on the back of the plate. (The back layer over the slot is cut away so you can see the nut.)

  ![The nut in the opening, with an arrow showing it pushed along the slot past the spring arms.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-latest-2-push-line-light.C5oPC5H4_Z1PSSds.webp)![The nut in the opening, with an arrow showing it pushed along the slot past the spring arms.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-latest-2-push-line-dark.6JIxs6_C_1J1Hlv.webp)![The nut in the opening, with an arrow showing it pushed along the slot past the spring arms.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-latest-2-push-shaded-light.-0JtvWlA_Z2qJsKz.webp)![The nut in the opening, with an arrow showing it pushed along the slot past the spring arms.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-latest-2-push-shaded-dark.CvJLVAoK_lnfWm.webp)

  Push it along the slot, past the spring arms.

* **Earlier base plates:** drop a nut into each slot opening and tip it into position on one side of the slot.

  ![The front of an earlier base plate at a slot end, top layer over the slot cut away. A square nut drops into the square opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-earlier-1-drop-line-light.DFVSuhFa_Z1QeiOd.webp)![The front of an earlier base plate at a slot end, top layer over the slot cut away. A square nut drops into the square opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-earlier-1-drop-line-dark.DEQnH83Y_Z1YbUMV.webp)![The front of an earlier base plate at a slot end, top layer over the slot cut away. A square nut drops into the square opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-earlier-1-drop-shaded-light.Cvot7yz0_Z8ciKA.webp)![The front of an earlier base plate at a slot end, top layer over the slot cut away. A square nut drops into the square opening.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-earlier-1-drop-shaded-dark.CyIkZKzQ_Z8c5AJ.webp)

  Earlier base plates: drop a nut into the slot opening.

  ![The nut in the opening of an earlier plate, with an arrow showing it moved into the slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-earlier-2-push-line-light.CnZbFuLC_Z1w5leh.webp)![The nut in the opening of an earlier plate, with an arrow showing it moved into the slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-earlier-2-push-line-dark.CbN58h0G_2psSwp.webp)![The nut in the opening of an earlier plate, with an arrow showing it moved into the slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-earlier-2-push-shaded-light.CgryOCPU_Z7dc3D.webp)![The nut in the opening of an earlier plate, with an arrow showing it moved into the slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-slot-nut-earlier-2-push-shaded-dark.0d6c8af5_1odXGy.webp)

  Tip it into position in the slot.

## Step 9: Attach towers to clusters

[Section titled “Step 9: Attach towers to clusters”](#step-9-attach-towers-to-clusters)

Attach each tower to its cluster first. Then attach the assembly to the nut in the base plate slot ([Step 10](/build/#step-10-install-towers-on-baseplates)).

Put an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw through the tower and into the square nut in the cluster, with the T10 driver. Tighten it a little to keep the cluster roughly in place. You adjust it later.

![An exploded view on one axis: an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw, the index tower (orange), and the finger cluster, with the square nut (blue) below its slot in the cluster.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-exploded-line-light.D3UZamSU_ZqXmPJ.webp)![An exploded view on one axis: an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw, the index tower (orange), and the finger cluster, with the square nut (blue) below its slot in the cluster.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-exploded-line-dark.BZnw6V76_bPIB2.webp)![An exploded view on one axis: an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw, the index tower (orange), and the finger cluster, with the square nut (blue) below its slot in the cluster.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-exploded-shaded-light.BLXRMY12_k9wr9.webp)![An exploded view on one axis: an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw, the index tower (orange), and the finger cluster, with the square nut (blue) below its slot in the cluster.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-exploded-shaded-dark.BxSwwCMI_ZwKxcx.webp)

The M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw passes through the tower and into the square nut in the cluster.

Make sure each tower goes in the right place:

* **Thumb:** the acute-angle tower, long side down.
* **Index fingers:** the tall oblique tower, tall side up.
* **Middle, ring and pinky:** the shorter, symmetric towers.

![Three stainless towers seen from the side, stacked: the thumb tower with its long side down, the tall index tower with its tall side up, and the shorter tower used for middle, ring and pinky.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-types-line-light.DZjV4Kcl_3lJe6.webp)![Three stainless towers seen from the side, stacked: the thumb tower with its long side down, the tall index tower with its tall side up, and the shorter tower used for middle, ring and pinky.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-types-line-dark.CJpsumc__Z77R95.webp)![Three stainless towers seen from the side, stacked: the thumb tower with its long side down, the tall index tower with its tall side up, and the shorter tower used for middle, ring and pinky.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-types-shaded-light.Dl7icsgU_ZiUpDM.webp)![Three stainless towers seen from the side, stacked: the thumb tower with its long side down, the tall index tower with its tall side up, and the shorter tower used for middle, ring and pinky.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-types-shaded-dark.BZB-Suk3_Z1JxBA3.webp)

Thumb: long side down. Index: tall side up. Middle, ring and pinky: the shorter towers.

![An index tower (orange) screwed to a finger cluster with an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-on-cluster-line-light.C39jfKQO_EuNiG.webp)![An index tower (orange) screwed to a finger cluster with an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-on-cluster-line-dark.mbyQgU8Q_Z1svtc8.webp)![An index tower (orange) screwed to a finger cluster with an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-on-cluster-shaded-light.CADLN8L__20cn4m.webp)![An index tower (orange) screwed to a finger cluster with an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-on-cluster-shaded-dark.DLIpIt_Z_29t5dB.webp)

## Step 10: Install towers on baseplates

[Section titled “Step 10: Install towers on baseplates”](#step-10-install-towers-on-baseplates)

1. Take a cluster and tower assembly. Feed the cluster’s FFC through the matching hole in the base plate.
2. Put an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw through the tower base and into the square nut in the base plate slot.
3. Tighten it enough to hold the tower. You’ll move the towers later to fit your hand ([Step 18](/build/#step-18-adjust-the-fit)), so don’t tighten them hard.

![An index tower and cluster lifted above the base plate. The cluster's FFC (blue) passes down through its hole in the plate, and an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw lines up with the tower base slot and the square nut (blue) in the plate slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-on-plate-line-light.Bf1DcRBs_Z2tb0EO.webp)![An index tower and cluster lifted above the base plate. The cluster's FFC (blue) passes down through its hole in the plate, and an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw lines up with the tower base slot and the square nut (blue) in the plate slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-on-plate-line-dark.DAnHIG_1_1Pj5Oe.webp)![An index tower and cluster lifted above the base plate. The cluster's FFC (blue) passes down through its hole in the plate, and an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw lines up with the tower base slot and the square nut (blue) in the plate slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-on-plate-shaded-light.ZW24pbAx_Z21NSm6.webp)![An index tower and cluster lifted above the base plate. The cluster's FFC (blue) passes down through its hole in the plate, and an M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw lines up with the tower base slot and the square nut (blue) in the plate slot.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tower-on-plate-shaded-dark.X-Wks4r3_Z2vz0Gb.webp)

Feed the FFC through the base plate, then screw the tower base to the square nut in the slot.

If you have a TrackPoint, trackball or touchpad, install it next: see [Steps 10a to 10c](/build/#steps-10a-to-10c-pointing-devices).

## Steps 10a to 10c: Pointing devices

[Section titled “Steps 10a to 10c: Pointing devices”](#steps-10a-to-10c-pointing-devices)

Use one pointing device per half. Connect its FFCs as in [Step 6](/build/#step-6-attach-ffcs).

### 10a TrackPoint

[Section titled “10a TrackPoint”](#10a-trackpoint)

* Attach a same-side FFC to the TrackPoint: unlatch, insert the contacts **up**, latch.
* Mount the TrackPoint in its holder with three M2 x 4 mm T6 thread-cutting screws.
* Attach the cover with two more M2 x 4 mm T6 screws.
* Route the cable with the finger cluster cables ([Step 10](/build/#step-10-install-towers-on-baseplates)).
* This half needs TrackPoint firmware. See [Step 15](/build/#step-15-flash-firmware-and-connect).
* The TrackPoint half must be the half you connect to your computer ([Step 15](/build/#step-15-flash-firmware-and-connect)).

![An exploded TrackPoint holder: the holder bottom, the TrackPoint module (blue) with its stick up, three M2 x 4 mm T6 screws, the cover, and two more M2 x 4 mm T6 screws for the cover, with dashed lines to their holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-trackpoint-exploded-line-light.zzR6q60w_iHyNB.webp)![An exploded TrackPoint holder: the holder bottom, the TrackPoint module (blue) with its stick up, three M2 x 4 mm T6 screws, the cover, and two more M2 x 4 mm T6 screws for the cover, with dashed lines to their holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-trackpoint-exploded-line-dark.Cd1uxale_9sswT.webp)![An exploded TrackPoint holder: the holder bottom, the TrackPoint module (blue) with its stick up, three M2 x 4 mm T6 screws, the cover, and two more M2 x 4 mm T6 screws for the cover, with dashed lines to their holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-trackpoint-exploded-shaded-light.C06Gl1C6_GH62V.webp)![An exploded TrackPoint holder: the holder bottom, the TrackPoint module (blue) with its stick up, three M2 x 4 mm T6 screws, the cover, and two more M2 x 4 mm T6 screws for the cover, with dashed lines to their holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-trackpoint-exploded-shaded-dark.Dfxfvqmw_qNOHT.webp)

TrackPoint holder: module stick up, held with three M2 x 4 mm T6 screws, then the cover with two more.

### 10b Trackball

[Section titled “10b Trackball”](#10b-trackball)

#### Trackball holder

[Section titled “Trackball holder”](#trackball-holder)

* Print the holder at 0.2 mm layer height with 6 or more walls. You can add supports under the large bridges, but in PLA the holders work fine without them.
* The holder takes four static bearing balls, 3.175 mm. Some older holder designs use 3 mm balls. See [Trackballs and static bearings](/build/#trackballs-and-static-bearings).

![The trackball holder from above with its cover beside it. Orange rings mark the four bearing balls: three in the cup and one in the keeper arm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-trackball-holder-line-light.CqM5IplY_Z1A00fV.webp)![The trackball holder from above with its cover beside it. Orange rings mark the four bearing balls: three in the cup and one in the keeper arm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-trackball-holder-line-dark.Cu_LhRXG_1hlSDT.webp)![The trackball holder from above with its cover beside it. Orange rings mark the four bearing balls: three in the cup and one in the keeper arm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-trackball-holder-shaded-light.wbJpeoHG_1DP6jg.webp)![The trackball holder from above with its cover beside it. Orange rings mark the four bearing balls: three in the cup and one in the keeper arm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-trackball-holder-shaded-dark.DxmRmhwj_29nLzJ.webp)

The four bearing balls: three in the cup and one in the keeper.

1. Remove the supports. Make sure the ball cavities are clear of stray material.
2. Put a small drop of medium CA glue in each bearing location, and drop a bearing into each.
3. After a moment, press each bearing into its seat with a screwdriver blade, so it seats fully.
4. Test the ball fit. The top arm (the keeper) should be very close to the ball but not touch it in normal use: 0 to 0.2 mm.
5. If needed, heat the keeper and bend it slightly to get the hold you want. Use hot water for PLA, or a heat gun on low for ABS. This is easier before the sensor is installed.

![A section through the holder and a 44 mm trackball (blue). A ring marks the small gap between the ball and the keeper's bearing ball.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-trackball-keeper-line-light.0WXLaGeC_ZTmTFO.webp)![A section through the holder and a 44 mm trackball (blue). A ring marks the small gap between the ball and the keeper's bearing ball.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-trackball-keeper-line-dark.BAyJTxqi_Zp4d4w.webp)![A section through the holder and a 44 mm trackball (blue). A ring marks the small gap between the ball and the keeper's bearing ball.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-trackball-keeper-shaded-light.Bq83HBob_Z27iJBl.webp)![A section through the holder and a 44 mm trackball (blue). A ring marks the small gap between the ball and the keeper's bearing ball.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-trackball-keeper-shaded-dark.KsU9n7lF_ZAWTmJ.webp)

The keeper sits very close to the ball without touching it: 0 to 0.2 mm.

If you don’t carry your Svalboard around and don’t tent it steeply, you don’t strictly need the keeper.

![The trackball holder, with the bearing balls in place. Labels show the direction the cover slides on and where the cable exits.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/trackball-holder.xz_InM7c_2aJlYW.webp)

#### Trackball PCBA

[Section titled “Trackball PCBA”](#trackball-pcba)

* Attach a same-side FFC to the trackball PCBA: unlatch, insert the contacts **down**, latch.

* Check which sensor the PCBA has. You need this to pick the firmware in [Step 15](/build/#step-15-flash-firmware-and-connect).

  * Current PCBAs use the **PMW3389**.
  * Older PCBAs may use the **PMW3360** (deprecated).
  * Look for silver marker on the PCBA, or read the tiny text on the sensor itself.

* Flashing the wrong image does no harm.

* Mount the trackball PCBA in its holder with the M2 x 4 mm T6 thread-cutting screws. Attach the cover.

* Route the cable with the finger cluster cables ([Step 10](/build/#step-10-install-towers-on-baseplates)).

* Connect the trackball cable to the 8-pin FFC connector marked “TrkPt”, “Trackball” or “Ball”, depending on your MCU: unlatch, insert the contacts down, latch.

### 10c Touchpad

[Section titled “10c Touchpad”](#10c-touchpad)

* The touchpad uses the same mounting rail as the trackball, so you can swap them.
* It needs MCU v3.1 or newer.
* Connect the 6-pin FFC to the touchpad: unlatch, insert the contacts **down**, latch.
* Connect the other end to the 6-pin “Azo” connector on the MCU: unlatch, insert the contacts **down**, latch.
* Mount the touchpad on the rail. The touchpad holder attaches to the base plate with a single M3 x 6 mm pan head T10 screw through the pointer slot. Use the T10 driver.
* Route the cable with the finger cluster cables ([Step 10](/build/#step-10-install-towers-on-baseplates)).
* This half needs touchpad firmware, or firmware that detects its pointing module automatically. See [Step 15](/build/#step-15-flash-firmware-and-connect).

## Step 11: Route cables

[Section titled “Step 11: Route cables”](#step-11-route-cables)

The photos show routing through the channels in the base plate. You don’t have to use the channels: connecting the cables directly, without them, is easier to work with in the long run. Either way, make sure every cable keeps the right orientation: contacts down at the MCU, blue stiffener up.

* You can put twists and creases in the FFCs wherever you like, under the PCBA or in the free sections below it.
* Don’t cut or tear the FFCs, and don’t drive screws into them.

The right half is shown.

![Three stages of routing the FFCs across the underside of the right base plate.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cables-through-baseplate-1.BvP7osEf_Z2j1VEv.webp)

![Three more stages of routing the FFCs on the right base plate, with the cables gathered toward the MCU position.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cables-through-baseplate-2.DEWLnSFL_Z1enolz.webp)

### Left half

[Section titled “Left half”](#left-half)

On the left half, the thumb FFC has to cross all the way to the opposite side.

![Routing the FFCs on the left base plate. The thumb FFC crosses to the far side before it reaches the MCU.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cables-left-hand.Dvs5kbtV_Z1N9Dz0.webp)

## Step 12: Install MCUs

[Section titled “Step 12: Install MCUs”](#step-12-install-mcus)

Screw the MCU (the main PCBA) to the base plate with four M3 6 mm thread-cutting screws. Then connect each FFC to its connector.

![The underside of a right base plate. Rings mark the four MCU screw bosses, with an M3 x 6 mm thread-cutting screw (orange) lined up over each.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-mcu-screws-line-light.CGC8IDBG_Z4aeiW.webp)![The underside of a right base plate. Rings mark the four MCU screw bosses, with an M3 x 6 mm thread-cutting screw (orange) lined up over each.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-mcu-screws-line-dark.-kES90ws_ZboqlK.webp)![The underside of a right base plate. Rings mark the four MCU screw bosses, with an M3 x 6 mm thread-cutting screw (orange) lined up over each.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-mcu-screws-shaded-light.3bCcunIa_Z1XLSyV.webp)![The underside of a right base plate. Rings mark the four MCU screw bosses, with an M3 x 6 mm thread-cutting screw (orange) lined up over each.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-mcu-screws-shaded-dark.Bwn_eJkA_esahK.webp)

Four screws hold each MCU.

*

The black latches on the connectors flip up to open and down to close.

* Every FFC connects to the MCU with the blue stiffener **up** and the metal contacts **down**: unlatch, insert, latch.
* On the TrackPoint PCBA end, the FFC connects with the metal contacts **up** and the blue stiffener down.

![Three photos of an MCU on a base plate, with the cluster FFCs being connected to its connectors.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/mcu-connect-1.i_i-HbO3_1rVCU1.webp)

![Three more photos of the FFCs connected to the MCU, with the slack folded under.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/mcu-connect-2.Z4uCShLp_1iwS0D.webp)

![Left: two photos of an MCU with all FFCs connected. A red line points to the pointing device cable. Right: a TrackPoint PCBA with its FFC, contacts up.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/mcu-connect-trackpoint.B8_CXfv6_1Msg9Q.webp)

## Step 13: Attach palm rest carriers

[Section titled “Step 13: Attach palm rest carriers”](#step-13-attach-palm-rest-carriers)

If you’re building the [sawed-off case](/build/#sawed-off-case), skip this step and Step 14.

The carrier holds the palm rest. Its cup takes the ball on the underside of the rest, and its two curved slots let it slide and turn on the base plate.

![The parts of a hemispherical palm rest, pulled apart from top to bottom: the M5 flat head screw (orange), the hemispherical top washer, the palm rest with the ball on its underside, the carrier with its cup, and the M5 square nut (orange).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-exploded-line-light.DaEOOYj6_Z2ffYv4.webp)![The parts of a hemispherical palm rest, pulled apart from top to bottom: the M5 flat head screw (orange), the hemispherical top washer, the palm rest with the ball on its underside, the carrier with its cup, and the M5 square nut (orange).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-exploded-line-dark.zlyEoOor_2hPO4x.webp)![The parts of a hemispherical palm rest, pulled apart from top to bottom: the M5 flat head screw (orange), the hemispherical top washer, the palm rest with the ball on its underside, the carrier with its cup, and the M5 square nut (orange).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-exploded-shaded-light.Dxj0U0ys_2va3UY.webp)![The parts of a hemispherical palm rest, pulled apart from top to bottom: the M5 flat head screw (orange), the hemispherical top washer, the palm rest with the ball on its underside, the carrier with its cup, and the M5 square nut (orange).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-exploded-shaded-dark.BdM27Y2Q_sTtdq.webp)

This step mounts the carrier and its nut, the bottom of the stack. Step 14 adds the palm rest, washer and screw on top.

1. Push an M5 square nut into the pocket on the underside of the carrier. It holds the palm rest’s center screw in Step 14.
2. Insert **two** square nuts into the palm rest slot in the base plate.
3. Place the carrier on the base plate, with its slots toward the finger clusters.
4. Put an M3x6 mm screw through each slot in the carrier and into a nut.
5. Tighten gently. It takes very little to hold the carrier. You set its final position in [Step 18](/build/#step-18-adjust-the-fit).

![A hemispherical palm rest carrier lifted above a cut-away corner of the base plate. Two M3 screws (orange) line up over the carrier's two curved slots and down to two M3 square nuts (orange) in the base plate's palm rest slot. An M5 square nut (blue) sits under the carrier, with an arrow up into its pocket.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-carrier-mount-line-light.vbfdb83h_Z26h7Su.webp)![A hemispherical palm rest carrier lifted above a cut-away corner of the base plate. Two M3 screws (orange) line up over the carrier's two curved slots and down to two M3 square nuts (orange) in the base plate's palm rest slot. An M5 square nut (blue) sits under the carrier, with an arrow up into its pocket.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-carrier-mount-line-dark.DifJXgny_1JNcSR.webp)![A hemispherical palm rest carrier lifted above a cut-away corner of the base plate. Two M3 screws (orange) line up over the carrier's two curved slots and down to two M3 square nuts (orange) in the base plate's palm rest slot. An M5 square nut (blue) sits under the carrier, with an arrow up into its pocket.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-carrier-mount-shaded-light.vBKSNApw_1FBe2f.webp)![A hemispherical palm rest carrier lifted above a cut-away corner of the base plate. Two M3 screws (orange) line up over the carrier's two curved slots and down to two M3 square nuts (orange) in the base plate's palm rest slot. An M5 square nut (blue) sits under the carrier, with an arrow up into its pocket.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-carrier-mount-shaded-dark.BjyV0OVx_Z2kgbe5.webp)

Push the M5 nut into the carrier's pocket, then screw the carrier to the two nuts in the palm rest slot, slots toward the clusters.

### Older builds: tripod carrier

[Section titled “Older builds: tripod carrier”](#older-builds-tripod-carrier)

The tripod carrier (also called the sled) mounts the same way, with two M3x6 mm screws through its straight slots into two square nuts. Washers are no longer needed, but you can use them for smoother sliding.

![A tripod carrier (sled) on the base plate, with one M3 x 6 mm screw (orange) in each of its two straight slots.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tripod-carrier-line-light.DGni8Pj__2gmBbi.webp)![A tripod carrier (sled) on the base plate, with one M3 x 6 mm screw (orange) in each of its two straight slots.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tripod-carrier-line-dark.D4cr0ppF_8vkKt.webp)![A tripod carrier (sled) on the base plate, with one M3 x 6 mm screw (orange) in each of its two straight slots.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tripod-carrier-shaded-light.BCfYM-gH_Z23UMHL.webp)![A tripod carrier (sled) on the base plate, with one M3 x 6 mm screw (orange) in each of its two straight slots.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tripod-carrier-shaded-dark.CJSKAiKw_2nTRlp.webp)

## Step 14: Attach palm rests

[Section titled “Step 14: Attach palm rests”](#step-14-attach-palm-rests)

The palm rest has a ball on its underside that sits in the cup of the carrier. One M5 flat head screw through the center holds it, so the rest can tilt in pitch and roll. The parts stack up as shown in the figure in [Step 13](/build/#step-13-attach-palm-rest-carriers).

1. Put the M5x16 mm flat head screw through the top washer, from the flat side.
2. Set the washer, round side down, in the recess in the top of the palm rest.
3. Set the palm rest on its carrier, with the ball in the cup and the window over the carrier slots.
4. Tighten the screw into the nut under the carrier with the 3 mm hex key. Leave it just loose enough to tilt the rest for now. You set the angle in [Step 18](/build/#step-18-adjust-the-fit).

![Cut-away side view of an assembled hemispherical palm rest. The M5 flat head screw passes through the top washer and the palm rest's ball, which sits in the carrier's cup, into the M5 square nut in the carrier.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-section-line-light.NJcmV7v2_INN2O.webp)![Cut-away side view of an assembled hemispherical palm rest. The M5 flat head screw passes through the top washer and the palm rest's ball, which sits in the carrier's cup, into the M5 square nut in the carrier.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-section-line-dark.sls5Ebsh_ZaX36O.webp)![Cut-away side view of an assembled hemispherical palm rest. The M5 flat head screw passes through the top washer and the palm rest's ball, which sits in the carrier's cup, into the M5 square nut in the carrier.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-section-shaded-light.COYHgC7U_1a1kH6.webp)![Cut-away side view of an assembled hemispherical palm rest. The M5 flat head screw passes through the top washer and the palm rest's ball, which sits in the carrier's cup, into the M5 square nut in the carrier.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-section-shaded-dark.BrjRny2c_26SfMV.webp)

The assembled stack, cut through the center screw.

![Both halves with hemispherical palm rests. On the near half, the center screw sits in the top of the rest. The far half shows the rest from the side, on its carrier.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/palm-rest-hemisphere-installed.BShyutqR_Z18A0oe.webp)

The rests ship on 9 mm carriers. For a higher or lower rest, print a carrier from 1 mm to 15 mm tall from the parts repository.

![Three hemispherical palm rest carriers side by side, from the side: 1 mm, 9 mm (the one that ships, in orange) and 15 mm tall.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-carrier-heights-line-light.CisQ5yEp_Z1Ksop9.webp)![Three hemispherical palm rest carriers side by side, from the side: 1 mm, 9 mm (the one that ships, in orange) and 15 mm tall.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-carrier-heights-line-dark.LI9oMUPV_5PFUq.webp)![Three hemispherical palm rest carriers side by side, from the side: 1 mm, 9 mm (the one that ships, in orange) and 15 mm tall.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-carrier-heights-shaded-light.CtUGw7wu_5M6xw.webp)![Three hemispherical palm rest carriers side by side, from the side: 1 mm, 9 mm (the one that ships, in orange) and 15 mm tall.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-carrier-heights-shaded-dark.CsSfBvY-_Z2kJ5eA.webp)

Carriers come in heights from 1 mm to 15 mm; 9 mm ships.

For a softer rest, add [Squishy Palmrests](https://svalboard.com/products/squishy-palmrests). Adhesive memory foam (1/4 inch) or adhesive-backed leather also work as padding. Foam is less durable.

![A Squishy Palmrest pad, a soft pad with a honeycomb grid on top, held above a hemispherical palm rest on its carrier, with an arrow pointing down onto the top of the palm rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-squishy-pad-line-light.D3Xv7wu4_1TMjjt.webp)![A Squishy Palmrest pad, a soft pad with a honeycomb grid on top, held above a hemispherical palm rest on its carrier, with an arrow pointing down onto the top of the palm rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-squishy-pad-line-dark.C8MuleKv_994qE.webp)![A Squishy Palmrest pad, a soft pad with a honeycomb grid on top, held above a hemispherical palm rest on its carrier, with an arrow pointing down onto the top of the palm rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-squishy-pad-shaded-light.oQ9xFSZV_12lbWb.webp)![A Squishy Palmrest pad, a soft pad with a honeycomb grid on top, held above a hemispherical palm rest on its carrier, with an arrow pointing down onto the top of the palm rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-squishy-pad-shaded-dark.CYoiQQPN_w1vwU.webp)

The pad goes on the top of the palm rest.

### Older builds: tripod palm rests

[Section titled “Older builds: tripod palm rests”](#older-builds-tripod-palm-rests-1)

The tripod palm rest drops into its sled on three legs. M2 x 4 mm T6 thread-cutting set screws clamp it at the sides. Don’t overtighten these screws.

![A tripod palm rest seated in its sled on the base plate.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/palm-rest-on-sled.2bkfPnbZ_pHIl2.webp)

You can shim a tripod rest to any height. The holes line up for 0 mm and 5 mm of lift with the default 5 mm shims. If you plan to add padding on top, you’ll probably want the low position. The fixing screws are the 4 mm M2 thread-cutting screws, the same as for the PCBAs.

![Exploded view of a tripod palm rest: the rest at the top, a 5 mm shim (orange) under each of its three legs, the sled with its three leg sockets, and an M2 x 4 mm screw (blue) beside each socket.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tripod-shims-line-light.Cz91DfOj_1tPNSi.webp)![Exploded view of a tripod palm rest: the rest at the top, a 5 mm shim (orange) under each of its three legs, the sled with its three leg sockets, and an M2 x 4 mm screw (blue) beside each socket.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tripod-shims-line-dark.DuncZki-_Z26szQI.webp)![Exploded view of a tripod palm rest: the rest at the top, a 5 mm shim (orange) under each of its three legs, the sled with its three leg sockets, and an M2 x 4 mm screw (blue) beside each socket.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tripod-shims-shaded-light.DCJZ3CUt_fiJ3c.webp)![Exploded view of a tripod palm rest: the rest at the top, a 5 mm shim (orange) under each of its three legs, the sled with its three leg sockets, and an M2 x 4 mm screw (blue) beside each socket.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tripod-shims-shaded-dark.7ZzLAyre_1aslSP.webp)

With the 5 mm shims in, the legs sit 5 mm higher and the M2 screws go in the upper holes.

## Step 15: Flash firmware and connect

[Section titled “Step 15: Flash firmware and connect”](#step-15-flash-firmware-and-connect)

Your MCUs ship with **no firmware**, and they aren’t set to left or right. Flash both.

### Pick your firmware

[Section titled “Pick your firmware”](#pick-your-firmware)

Svalboard runs **Svalboard QMK**, configured with **Keybard**.

1. Go to the latest release: <https://github.com/svalboard/qmk/releases/latest>
2. Download one `sval` `.uf2` file for each half. Pick by side, and by the pointing device on that half (none, trackball, TrackPoint or touchpad). The full list of files is in [Firmware files](/firmware/#firmware-files).

* Use the newest release, and the same release on both halves.
* The `blank` files have no keys assigned. Use them only for the cluster test in [Step 7](/build/#test-the-clusters-recommended).
* Flashing the wrong image does no harm. Flash the right one and try again.

### Flash each half

[Section titled “Flash each half”](#flash-each-half)

Do this once for each half.

1. Connect the half to your computer with a USB-C cable in the port marked **U**.
2. Double-tap the **reset** button on the bottom of the half.
3. A drive named **RPI-RP2** appears.
4. Copy that half’s `.uf2` file onto the drive.
5. The half restarts by itself and the drive disappears. That half is done.

Flashing resets the layout to the default. Later, export a `.svil` from Keybard before you flash, and import it afterward. More detail: [Flashing firmware](/firmware/#flashing-firmware).

#### Staying on Vial

[Section titled “Staying on Vial”](#staying-on-vial)

Svalboard’s Vial firmware also works with the board. To use it, flash the `v2025-11-01` files from <https://github.com/svalboard/vial-qmk/releases> and configure the board with Vial (<https://vial.rocks>). The rest of this guide uses Keybard.

### Connect the cables

[Section titled “Connect the cables”](#connect-the-cables)

* Use the two USB-C cables from the kit.
* **Split cable:** the shorter cable joins the two ports marked **S** (or ↔).
* **Computer cable:** the longer cable goes from the port marked **U** on one half to your computer. That half is the main half.
* If you have a TrackPoint, the TrackPoint half must be the main half.
* Otherwise, make the half with your main pointing device the main half. The main half performs better.
* You can connect or disconnect the split cable while the board is plugged in.

### Connect Keybard

[Section titled “Connect Keybard”](#connect-keybard)

1. Open <https://keybard.svalboard.com> in Chrome or Edge on a desktop computer.
2. Choose **Connect Keyboard**, then pick your Svalboard in the browser’s list.
3. Your layout loads. You can now edit it. Changes apply right away, with no flashing.
4. Keybard backs up each board automatically. After you change your layout, also choose **Export Layout** and keep the `.svil` file somewhere safe.

See [Keybard](/keybard/) for more.

#### On Linux

[Section titled “On Linux”](#on-linux)

Linux won’t let the browser open the board until you add a udev rule. See [Linux: the udev rule](/firmware/#linux-the-udev-rule).

## Step 16: Test all keys

[Section titled “Step 16: Test all keys”](#step-16-test-all-keys)

Do this before you screw on the back cover.

1. Open [Keybard](/keybard/) and connect ([Step 15](/build/#connect-keybard)).
2. In the editor toolbar, choose **Matrix Tester**.
3. Press each finger key in every direction, and each thumb key. Hold each press for a moment.
4. Check that every key activates, and that the key that lights up is the one you pressed.
5. Use **Clear Matrix** to start over. This doesn’t change your layout.
6. Choose **Exit Matrix Tester** when you’re done.

If you have a pointing device, move it and check that the pointer moves.

### If a key doesn’t register

[Section titled “If a key doesn’t register”](#if-a-key-doesnt-register)

* Check that the key moves freely.
* Check that its flag is intact and opaque. Light filaments need silver marker ([Step 5](/build/#step-5-ink-the-key-flags)).
* Check that the PCBA sits flat in the cluster, including the bottom-left corner ([Step 7](/build/#step-7-install-pcbas-and-test)).
* Check that the FFC is fully inserted and latched at both ends, contacts down.
* If the Matrix Tester shows the key but typing is wrong, the switch is fine. Check that key’s layer and binding.

### On Vial

[Section titled “On Vial”](#on-vial)

On Svalboard’s Vial firmware, use Vial’s **Matrix Tester** tab instead.

## Step 17: Install back cover and feet

[Section titled “Step 17: Install back cover and feet”](#step-17-install-back-cover-and-feet)

When every key works ([Step 16](/build/#step-16-test-all-keys)):

1. Screw on the back cover with 7 M3 6 mm screws per side.
2. Add 4 rubber feet per side, in the holes closest to the four corners.
3. Trim the feet on the thin side of the case, so they don’t press against the base plate and deform it. Leave enough material that they stay in place.

![A half turned upside down and pulled apart: the back cover lifted off the base plate, with seven M3 x 6 mm screws (orange) lined up over its screw holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-back-cover-screws-line-light._E4pBdSr_Z1pcHQa.webp)![A half turned upside down and pulled apart: the back cover lifted off the base plate, with seven M3 x 6 mm screws (orange) lined up over its screw holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-back-cover-screws-line-dark.BNP0Ss3g_Z214NeM.webp)![A half turned upside down and pulled apart: the back cover lifted off the base plate, with seven M3 x 6 mm screws (orange) lined up over its screw holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-back-cover-screws-shaded-light.B_NOih-l_2mmD3j.webp)![A half turned upside down and pulled apart: the back cover lifted off the base plate, with seven M3 x 6 mm screws (orange) lined up over its screw holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-back-cover-screws-shaded-dark.DyftLx9Z_2voYW0.webp)

Seven M3 x 6 mm screws hold the back cover to the base plate.

If the board rocks, shave the bottoms of the feet with a craft knife. The silicone is very soft and easy to trim. You can also work on reducing warping in your prints.

### Feet sizes

[Section titled “Feet sizes”](#feet-sizes)

* Recent cases have 4.8 mm holes for the larger rubber feet.
* Case version 1.2.6 and later also fit the small plug feet: 6 mm across, about 3 mm long, in soft 70A silicone. They lower the stack by more than a millimeter. On an older case, drill 3 mm holes to fit them.

![The bottom of a right back case. Rubber feet (orange) sit in the four 4.8 mm holes closest to the corners, and a line points to one of the seven case screw counterbores.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-back-cover-feet-line-light.Dur0UuKr_Z1bEtfh.webp)![The bottom of a right back case. Rubber feet (orange) sit in the four 4.8 mm holes closest to the corners, and a line points to one of the seven case screw counterbores.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-back-cover-feet-line-dark.DXsnF-O__Z1fYhVH.webp)![The bottom of a right back case. Rubber feet (orange) sit in the four 4.8 mm holes closest to the corners, and a line points to one of the seven case screw counterbores.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-back-cover-feet-shaded-light.HMA4QrX-_6JWD0.webp)![The bottom of a right back case. Rubber feet (orange) sit in the four 4.8 mm holes closest to the corners, and a line points to one of the seven case screw counterbores.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-back-cover-feet-shaded-dark.DqLgZWh7_Z20SnmH.webp)

## Step 18: Adjust the fit

[Section titled “Step 18: Adjust the fit”](#step-18-adjust-the-fit)

Adjust each part of the Svalboard to fit your hands. You’ll keep making small adjustments over the first days or weeks of use. This is normal. Shaping the palm rests can also make typing much more comfortable.

**Don’t overtighten.** The screws go into metal nuts, but there’s plastic between them. Too much force can crack or break it.

### Palm rest

[Section titled “Palm rest”](#palm-rest)

The carrier slides in X and Y on the base plate. Keep it square to the plate, slots running north–south. The palm rest itself turns on the carrier for yaw and tilts for pitch and roll.

![A palm rest carrier on the base plate, with its two screws. Arrows show it sliding along the slot (Y) and across it (X).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-palm-motion-1-slide-line-light.D9N9UeG5_DiSlI.webp)![A palm rest carrier on the base plate, with its two screws. Arrows show it sliding along the slot (Y) and across it (X).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-palm-motion-1-slide-line-dark.CZje6M4z_8OEMT.webp)![A palm rest carrier on the base plate, with its two screws. Arrows show it sliding along the slot (Y) and across it (X).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-palm-motion-1-slide-shaded-light.DlOxYtv9_1Dy46m.webp)![A palm rest carrier on the base plate, with its two screws. Arrows show it sliding along the slot (Y) and across it (X).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-palm-motion-1-slide-shaded-dark.DmMHhGk1_Z1vHuKl.webp)

Loosen the two carrier screws to slide the carrier. Keep it square to the base plate.

![A hemispherical palm rest on its carrier. Arrows show it turning on the carrier (Yaw), tilting front to back (Pitch) and side to side (Roll). Lines point to the center screw and to the carrier screws, seen through the window in the rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-palm-motion-2-tilt-line-light.UIXEWgm9_Z1zjFMd.webp)![A hemispherical palm rest on its carrier. Arrows show it turning on the carrier (Yaw), tilting front to back (Pitch) and side to side (Roll). Lines point to the center screw and to the carrier screws, seen through the window in the rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-palm-motion-2-tilt-line-dark.BICK3oKj_Z1q1uvT.webp)![A hemispherical palm rest on its carrier. Arrows show it turning on the carrier (Yaw), tilting front to back (Pitch) and side to side (Roll). Lines point to the center screw and to the carrier screws, seen through the window in the rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-palm-motion-2-tilt-shaded-light.oq_Vejdk_Z2bJlU7.webp)![A hemispherical palm rest on its carrier. Arrows show it turning on the carrier (Yaw), tilting front to back (Pitch) and side to side (Roll). Lines point to the center screw and to the carrier screws, seen through the window in the rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-palm-motion-2-tilt-shaded-dark.DKOZ2uu4_Z9GIkC.webp)

Loosen the center screw to turn the rest (yaw) and tilt it (pitch and roll).

1. Reach the two carrier screws through the window in the palm rest, and loosen them slightly.
2. With a relaxed hand, your fingers should rest comfortably on the center keys. Slide the carrier to get a good starting position, keeping it square to the base plate. You can always tweak it later.
3. The base knuckles of each hand usually rest just in front of the front edge of the palm rest.
4. Tighten both carrier screws gently snug to fix the position.
5. To set yaw, pitch and roll, loosen the large center screw slightly with the 3 mm hex key. Turn the rest to the angle your hand wants, tilt it until your palm lies flat on it, then tighten the center screw firmly.

![Close-up of a hemispherical palm rest. The center screw sits in its washer, and the two carrier screws show through the window above it.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/palm-rest-hemisphere-screws.B5dfb37u_Z2n2rWq.webp)

#### Older builds: tripod palm rests

[Section titled “Older builds: tripod palm rests”](#older-builds-tripod-palm-rests-2)

Loosen both carrier screws slightly, slide and turn the carrier as above, then tighten the screws gently snug. To change the height, add or remove shims under the legs ([Step 14](/build/#step-14-attach-palm-rests)).

![A tripod palm rest carrier on the base plate, with its two screws in the carrier slots.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/fit-palm-rest.CWOUh0m5_1iK0KO.webp)

### Finger clusters

[Section titled “Finger clusters”](#finger-clusters)

Each cluster moves in X, Y and yaw.

1. Loosen the tower base screw (M3 x 6 mm pan head, T10) slightly with the T10 driver.
2. Tighten it gently to test and fine-tune.
3. After you set the palm rest, adjust how far forward or back each cluster sits, so each finger feels equally relaxed. Fingers should rest only on the center keys, and on the South keys if you prefer.
4. Tighten snug, without overdoing it, to fix the position.

To move one finger farther away than its slot allows, move the other fingers closer instead, and move the palm rest farther from the clusters to make room.

![An index tower (orange) and finger cluster on a corner of the base plate. A line points to the tower base screw; arrows show the cluster moving along the tower foot (Y), along the plate slot (X), and turning (Yaw).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-fit-cluster-xy-line-light.BN-xozLS_1tJcdA.webp)![An index tower (orange) and finger cluster on a corner of the base plate. A line points to the tower base screw; arrows show the cluster moving along the tower foot (Y), along the plate slot (X), and turning (Yaw).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-fit-cluster-xy-line-dark.B0Q9D_fY_ZDR6MB.webp)![An index tower (orange) and finger cluster on a corner of the base plate. A line points to the tower base screw; arrows show the cluster moving along the tower foot (Y), along the plate slot (X), and turning (Yaw).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-fit-cluster-xy-shaded-light.BT8rnCKL_Z1h9zPl.webp)![An index tower (orange) and finger cluster on a corner of the base plate. A line points to the tower base screw; arrows show the cluster moving along the tower foot (Y), along the plate slot (X), and turning (Yaw).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-fit-cluster-xy-shaded-dark.B8RNhdw8_2av839.webp)

### Height and roll

[Section titled “Height and roll”](#height-and-roll)

1. Loosen the cluster height screws (M3 x 6 mm pan head, T10) slightly with the T10 driver. The washer may bind a little. Don’t unscrew too far. Wiggle it gently, or lift the edge of the washer to break it free of the plastic.
2. **Roll:** set it so each finger presses the East and West keys equally easily. If you have to favor one side, make the inboard key slightly higher, so it’s easier to press: West on the right hand, East on the left hand.
3. **Height:** set it so each finger rests with the same light pressure on its center key, without touching any other key.

![A finger cluster on its tower, seen from behind the tower. A line points to the cluster height screw; arrows show the cluster sliding up and down the tower (Z) and turning on the screw (Roll).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-fit-height-roll-line-light.mJ4Ty2VK_Z1tEtzI.webp)![A finger cluster on its tower, seen from behind the tower. A line points to the cluster height screw; arrows show the cluster sliding up and down the tower (Z) and turning on the screw (Roll).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-fit-height-roll-line-dark.D-tSjmzU_af3zu.webp)![A finger cluster on its tower, seen from behind the tower. A line points to the cluster height screw; arrows show the cluster sliding up and down the tower (Z) and turning on the screw (Roll).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-fit-height-roll-shaded-light.CYknFwkn_2wYsSn.webp)![A finger cluster on its tower, seen from behind the tower. A line points to the cluster height screw; arrows show the cluster sliding up and down the tower (Z) and turning on the screw (Roll).](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-fit-height-roll-shaded-dark.DTmbiRPU_ZdpScf.webp)

### Palm rest shaping (PLA only)

[Section titled “Palm rest shaping (PLA only)”](#palm-rest-shaping-pla-only)

Watch the [palm rest shaping video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=feAgCKpLzhQ).

* Only shape the palm rest while it’s attached to the carrier. On a tripod rest, this keeps the legs in the right places.
* Dip the area you want to shape in water at about 90 °C. Swish it gently for 5 to 10 seconds until it’s pliable.
* Quickly shake off the hot water and form it to your hand. It cools and hardens quickly.
* Work a little at a time. Don’t rush, and don’t force a bend, or the layers may split.
* Keep a bowl of cool water nearby. If the plastic gets too soft, dip it to set the shape quickly.

## Step 19: Enjoy!

[Section titled “Step 19: Enjoy!”](#step-19-enjoy)

* Your Svalboard starts with the default QWERTY layout.
* To change keys, layers, macros, combos or tap dances, use [Keybard](/keybard/): <https://keybard.svalboard.com>
* For other letter layouts and number layers, open Keybard’s **Layouts** panel and drag a layer onto yours. It has Dvorak, Colemak, the Hands Down variants (HD Promethium, HD Neu), Graphite, and NavNAS number layers.
* Read the [Svalboard Manual](https://svalboard.com/manual) to get the most from your Svalboard.
* Questions? Ask on the [Svalboard Discord](https://www.svalboard.com/discord), or email <support@svalboard.com>.

### Thumb cluster layer lights

[Section titled “Thumb cluster layer lights”](#thumb-cluster-layer-lights)

Thumb clusters in kits shipped after May 2024 have an RGB layer light. It shows the active layer. The default colors are:

* Green: layer 0 (base)
* Orange: layer 1 (NavNAS)
* Azure: layer 2 (Function)
* Magenta: layer 15 (mouse layer)

You can change each layer’s color in Keybard. On Svalboard’s Vial firmware, colors are set in the firmware source.

If you print the thumb cluster in a dark color, turn the brightness up, or print the diffuser in white. The diffuser is a separate part in the STEP file.

### Brightness

[Section titled “Brightness”](#brightness)

* Set the brightness in Keybard: click the color dot beside the layer name, then the gear button (**Custom layer color**). Select **LED color** and drag **Brightness**. Choose **Apply**. It applies to every layer.
* Or add **Bright +** and **Bright -** to keys (Keybard’s **Special Keys** panel, **Backlight and RGB Keys**), then press them on the board.
* **RGB Toggle** turns the layer lights on and off.

![The same right thumb cluster with its keys, shown twice side by side. On the left, labeled Dim, the layer light window between the Nail and Knuckle keys glows faint green. On the right, labeled Bright, the window glows bright green and lights up the cluster around it.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-led-brightness-line-light.Bfa5hv0A_1VqF9a.webp)![The same right thumb cluster with its keys, shown twice side by side. On the left, labeled Dim, the layer light window between the Nail and Knuckle keys glows faint green. On the right, labeled Bright, the window glows bright green and lights up the cluster around it.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-led-brightness-line-dark.BHlci8CT_Z1T90AL.webp)![The same right thumb cluster with its keys, shown twice side by side. On the left, labeled Dim, the layer light window between the Nail and Knuckle keys glows faint green. On the right, labeled Bright, the window glows bright green and lights up the cluster around it.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-led-brightness-shaded-light.CMr_hUhH_Z19DbnT.webp)![The same right thumb cluster with its keys, shown twice side by side. Before and after turning up the brightness.

# Firmware

> Flash, recover and get to know Svalboard QMK firmware.

## Flashing firmware

[Section titled “Flashing firmware”](#flashing-firmware)

Both firmwares install the same way: copy a `.uf2` file onto the board.

**Flashing resets your layout and settings to the firmware’s default layout.** Back up first and restore afterward.

1. **Back up your layout.** In Keybard, choose **Export Layout** and save a `.svil` file. On Vial, save a `.vil`.
2. Download the right file for **each half**: the side (left or right) and, on the current firmware, the pointing module on that half (see [Firmware files](/firmware/#firmware-files), or [Vial firmware files](/vial/#vial-firmware-files) for Vial).
3. Plug **one half** into your computer by its **U** port.
4. Press its **RESET** button twice quickly, within half a second. A drive named **RPI-RP2** appears.
5. Copy that half’s `.uf2` onto the drive. The half restarts by itself and the drive disappears. This is normal.
6. Move the USB cable to the other half and repeat with its file.
7. Plug in normally. In Keybard, choose **Import Layout** and pick your `.svil`.

Both halves must run the same release. Don’t press keys, especially thumb keys, while the board starts.

New microcontrollers, in a kit or as spares, ship with no firmware and are not set to a side. Flash each one with the file for the half it goes in.

## What’s new compared with Vial

[Section titled “What’s new compared with Vial”](#whats-new-compared-with-vial)

Svalboard QMK is the current firmware, `svalboard/qmk`, release **vLaunch2**. You configure it with [Keybard](/keybard/) in Chrome or Edge.

Already in Svalboard’s Vial firmware, now edited in Keybard:

* tap dances, combos, key overrides, alternate-repeat keys, macros and QMK settings
* DPI, scrolling and Sniper keys
* automouse toggle and timeout
* TrackPoint recalibration

New in Svalboard QMK:

* **256 entries** each for tap dances, combos, key overrides, macros, alternate-repeat keys and leader sequences.
* **Leader sequences**: a Leader key, then up to five keys, triggers an action.
* **Layer colors and LED brightness set from Keybard** (see [Layer lights and brightness](/keybard/#layer-lights-and-brightness)).
* **Board identity**: each board keeps its identity and can have a name.
* **Sniper toggle**: slow movement without holding a key.
* **Boost**: 2x, 3x or 5x faster movement, held or toggled.
* **Per-pointer automouse**, with an activation threshold and decay.
* **Natural scrolling**.
* **Idle power** settings.
* **Protocol additions**: host apps can read and control layer state.

Settings are stored in two checked copies, so a bad read doesn’t wipe your layout.

Changed: **Chordal Hold** replaces Achordion and is on by default. It is similar but not identical; check your mod-taps after moving.

Keybard also adds automatic backups, layer reordering, a saved default layer, a layouts library, printable layers and the Keybard Overlay app.

To move your board over, see [Moving from Vial](/firmware/#moving-from-vial).

## Firmware files

[Section titled “Firmware files”](#firmware-files)

Download from the [vLaunch2 release](https://github.com/svalboard/qmk/releases/tag/vLaunch2). Pick one file per half, by the module on that half:

| Module on that half                           | Left                                                 | Right                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| None                                          | `svalboard_left_sval_vLaunch2.uf2`                   | `svalboard_right_sval_vLaunch2.uf2`                   |
| None, blank keymap                            | `svalboard_left_blank_vLaunch2.uf2`                  | `svalboard_right_blank_vLaunch2.uf2`                  |
| Trackball                                     | `svalboard_trackball_pmw3389_left_sval_vLaunch2.uf2` | `svalboard_trackball_pmw3389_right_sval_vLaunch2.uf2` |
| TrackPoint                                    | `svalboard_trackpoint_left_sval_vLaunch2.uf2`        | `svalboard_trackpoint_right_sval_vLaunch2.uf2`        |
| Touchpad                                      | `svalboard_azoteq_left_sval_vLaunch2.uf2`            | `svalboard_azoteq_right_sval_vLaunch2.uf2`            |
| Trackball, early 2024 units only (deprecated) | `svalboard_trackball_pmw3360_left_sval_vLaunch2.uf2` | `svalboard_trackball_pmw3360_right_sval_vLaunch2.uf2` |

The `blank` files have no keys assigned. Builders use them to test keys without typing anything.

Flash as in [Flashing firmware](/firmware/#flashing-firmware). Flashing resets your layout to the default, so export a `.svil` first and import it afterward.

## Recovery

[Section titled “Recovery”](#recovery)

* **“Your keyboard’s settings were reset”**: the board couldn’t read its settings and started from defaults. Import your `.svil`, or restore a backup from before the reset in **Settings → Backups**.
* **“Your keyboard can’t save changes”**: export your current work, unplug the board, plug it back in, reconnect and make the change again.
* **After any reset**: restart the board before making new edits.
* **Keybard won’t connect**: use Chrome or Edge, a USB data cable, and close other configuration apps. On Linux, add the udev rule (see [Linux: the udev rule](/firmware/#linux-the-udev-rule)).
* **Board won’t start or a half is stuck**: reflash both halves with matching vLaunch2 files (see [Flashing firmware](/firmware/#flashing-firmware)), then import your `.svil`.

For hardware problems, see [Troubleshooting](/hardware/#troubleshooting).

## Known limitations

[Section titled “Known limitations”](#known-limitations)

* Alternate-repeat keys: modifier matching and “default to alternate” have known defects. Test custom mappings.
* Release a tap-dance key before changing its action.
* Auto Shift isn’t in the standard firmware.
* Automatic backups live in one browser. Keep an exported `.svil` too.

## Linux: the udev rule

[Section titled “Linux: the udev rule”](#linux-the-udev-rule)

Linux lets only root open the keyboard until you add a udev rule. Without it, Keybard and Keybard Overlay can see the board but can’t open it. Older Svalboard rules matched a Vial serial number that current firmware no longer reports, so many people hit this after a firmware update.

This rule covers every Svalboard QMK firmware file:

```plaintext
KERNEL=="hidraw*", SUBSYSTEM=="hidraw", ATTRS{idVendor}=="303a", ATTRS{idProduct}=="404[4-9a-d]", MODE="0660", TAG+="uaccess"
```

To install it, run these commands in a terminal:

```sh
sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/60-svalboard.rules > /dev/null <<'EOF'
KERNEL=="hidraw*", SUBSYSTEM=="hidraw", ATTRS{idVendor}=="303a", ATTRS{idProduct}=="404[4-9a-d]", MODE="0660", TAG+="uaccess"
EOF
sudo udevadm control --reload
sudo udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=hidraw
```

Then unplug the board, plug it back in, and connect again. If you have an old Svalboard rule in another file under `/etc/udev/rules.d/`, delete it.

When Keybard hits this problem, it shows these same commands, with the rule above, ready to copy. If you installed an older Keybard command that names a single product ID, replace it with this rule.

### USB IDs

[Section titled “USB IDs”](#usb-ids)

The product ID for each firmware file is in [USB IDs](/reference/usb-ids/).

## Moving from Vial

[Section titled “Moving from Vial”](#moving-from-vial)

The firmware does **not** bring your Vial settings across. Flashing resets the board to the default layout. Keybard can import your Vial `.vil` to restore it.

1. In Vial, save your layout as a `.vil`. Keep it unchanged.
2. Write down anything you rely on that a `.vil` doesn’t hold: DPI, scrolling, automouse and layer colors (see [What a .vil doesn’t hold](/firmware/#what-a-vil-doesnt-hold)).
3. Flash both halves with the vLaunch2 files (see [Firmware files](/firmware/#firmware-files) and [Flashing firmware](/firmware/#flashing-firmware)).
4. Open <https://keybard.svalboard.com> in Chrome or Edge and choose **Connect Keyboard**.
5. Choose **Import Layout** and pick your `.vil`. Read the review, then apply it. This restores your layout, macros, tap dances, combos, key overrides and QMK settings.
6. Set DPI, scrolling, automouse and layer colors again in Keybard.
7. Check every layer, your macros, your modifier swaps and your mod-tap feel (Chordal Hold replaces Achordion).
8. Export a `.svil` backup once it all works.

The first start after flashing takes a few seconds longer while the board sets up its settings storage.

If you’d rather start fresh, skip the import and use Keybard’s **Layouts** panel for letter and NavNAS layers (see [Start from a layout Svalboard provides](/keybard/#start-from-a-layout-svalboard-provides)).

## Going back to Vial

[Section titled “Going back to Vial”](#going-back-to-vial)

1. In Keybard, export your setup twice with **Export Layout**: once as **Svalboard (.svil) - Native Format**, and once as **Vial (.vil) - Legacy Compatibility** for Vial.
2. Flash both halves with the Vial v2025-11-01 files (see [Vial firmware files](/vial/#vial-firmware-files) and [Flashing firmware](/firmware/#flashing-firmware)). This resets the board to Vial’s default layout.
3. Open Vial and load your `.vil`.

Settings that only exist in Svalboard QMK (leaders, Boost, entries above Vial’s limits) don’t carry back. See also [What a .vil doesn’t hold](/firmware/#what-a-vil-doesnt-hold).

## What a .vil doesn’t hold

[Section titled “What a .vil doesn’t hold”](#what-a-vil-doesnt-hold)

A `.vil` file doesn’t hold DPI, scrolling, automouse, layer colors, names or cluster selections. Set those again after moving in either direction.

See [Moving from Vial](/firmware/#moving-from-vial) and [Going back to Vial](/firmware/#going-back-to-vial).

# Hardware

> The two halves, their ports and keys, mounting and tenting, care, opening the case and repairs.

## The halves

[Section titled “The halves”](#the-halves)

![Both halves from above, labeled: towers, finger clusters, trackball, thumb cluster, palm rest, carrier and baseplate.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/halves-overview.DqcoMqwG_Z13PKd6.webp)

![The finger end of a right half's case, from below. The U (USB) port and the S (split) port are side by side in the end wall, and the RESET button hole is in the bottom.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ports-reset-line-light.CWzu6Ew4_ZQBAQI.webp)![The finger end of a right half's case, from below. The U (USB) port and the S (split) port are side by side in the end wall, and the RESET button hole is in the bottom.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ports-reset-line-dark.BTCZb2dA_Z24hQ7y.webp)![The finger end of a right half's case, from below. The U (USB) port and the S (split) port are side by side in the end wall, and the RESET button hole is in the bottom.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ports-reset-shaded-light.DQuNDayU_2npvdO.webp)![The finger end of a right half's case, from below. The U (USB) port and the S (split) port are side by side in the end wall, and the RESET button hole is in the bottom.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-ports-reset-shaded-dark.OSxShWLl_TjToW.webp)

Right half shown; the left half is its mirror image.

Each half has its own RP2040 microcontroller and its own firmware. You flash each half with the file for its side (left or right). Copying a firmware file does not change which side a half is.

* **U port**: the USB port, to your computer.
* **S port** (or **↔**): the split port, for the split cable to the other half. You can connect and disconnect the split cable while the board is plugged in.
* **RESET button**: on the bottom of each half. A double press starts bootloader mode (see [Flashing firmware](/firmware/#flashing-firmware)).

## Keys

[Section titled “Keys”](#keys)

![A finger cluster with its keys labeled: North at the back, East, South, West, and the Center key in the middle, plus the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-finger-cluster-keys-line-light.BxJBo7jo_Z1jBbYr.webp)![A finger cluster with its keys labeled: North at the back, East, South, West, and the Center key in the middle, plus the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-finger-cluster-keys-line-dark.ByC0_wUl_ZN6l2v.webp)![A finger cluster with its keys labeled: North at the back, East, South, West, and the Center key in the middle, plus the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-finger-cluster-keys-shaded-light.Dr3rwVlo_Z1hcL65.webp)![A finger cluster with its keys labeled: North at the back, East, South, West, and the Center key in the middle, plus the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-finger-cluster-keys-shaded-dark.D-ibojLQ_2rm15I.webp)

Each finger has a **5-key cluster**: North, South, East, West, and a Center key pressed down. This is the standard cluster.

![A right thumb cluster seen almost level from its outer side, keys labeled: the Nail and Knuckle keys in front, the Pad key behind, whose sloped top runs on into the Knuckle top as one line rising toward the Up key, the Up key, the Down key between them, the layer LED, and the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-line-light.DhxyIN4r_RnwvJ.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen almost level from its outer side, keys labeled: the Nail and Knuckle keys in front, the Pad key behind, whose sloped top runs on into the Knuckle top as one line rising toward the Up key, the Up key, the Down key between them, the layer LED, and the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-line-dark.DDzCwfv7_1Q8N6f.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen almost level from its outer side, keys labeled: the Nail and Knuckle keys in front, the Pad key behind, whose sloped top runs on into the Knuckle top as one line rising toward the Up key, the Up key, the Down key between them, the layer LED, and the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-shaded-light.DRyMLY9h_27UYIk.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen almost level from its outer side, keys labeled: the Nail and Knuckle keys in front, the Pad key behind, whose sloped top runs on into the Knuckle top as one line rising toward the Up key, the Up key, the Down key between them, the layer LED, and the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-shaded-dark.Drw6YBLA_1vTUn.webp)

Each thumb has six keys: **Pad, Knuckle, Nail, Up, Down and Double Down**. Double Down is a switch under the Down key: press Down all the way through.

That gives **52 keys** in total, each a few millimeters from your fingers.

For more reach, choose the **6-key finger cluster**, which adds a second South key under each finger that has one. Put it on any or all fingers for 56 to 60 keys. Every Svalboard firmware supports it. In Keybard, choose the clusters your board has in **Settings → Fragments** (see [Fragments](/keybard/#fragments-your-finger-clusters)).

![A 6-key finger cluster body with its key slots labeled: North, East, West, Center, South, and the Second South (2S) slot, ringed, behind South.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-6key-cluster-line-light.Bi4YZ6rB_rcsuG.webp)![A 6-key finger cluster body with its key slots labeled: North, East, West, Center, South, and the Second South (2S) slot, ringed, behind South.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-6key-cluster-line-dark.CwbkWIrO_1EPgLG.webp)![A 6-key finger cluster body with its key slots labeled: North, East, West, Center, South, and the Second South (2S) slot, ringed, behind South.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-6key-cluster-shaded-light.D2-L5GqL_Z1fKox5.webp)![A 6-key finger cluster body with its key slots labeled: North, East, West, Center, South, and the Second South (2S) slot, ringed, behind South.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-6key-cluster-shaded-dark.PN4WsTA4_oVJHc.webp)

The 6-key cluster adds a Second South key behind South.

## Mounting and tenting

[Section titled “Mounting and tenting”](#mounting-and-tenting)

Each half has two M5 inserts at the inner edge and a ¼”-20 insert at the center.

![The bottom of the right back case. Two M5 inserts (orange) sit near the inner edge and a 1/4-20 insert (blue) in the middle.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-inserts-back-case-line-light.BuNTBLnD_2c1prR.webp)![The bottom of the right back case. Two M5 inserts (orange) sit near the inner edge and a 1/4-20 insert (blue) in the middle.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-inserts-back-case-line-dark.CtQ95egJ_Z18e1eL.webp)![The bottom of the right back case. Two M5 inserts (orange) sit near the inner edge and a 1/4-20 insert (blue) in the middle.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-inserts-back-case-shaded-light.DB-Er1TE_Z1TiMgI.webp)![The bottom of the right back case. Two M5 inserts (orange) sit near the inner edge and a 1/4-20 insert (blue) in the middle.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-inserts-back-case-shaded-dark.UCuhdvXW_Z1Ad86G.webp)

Back case, bottom: two M5 inserts for screw-in legs and one 1/4-20 insert in the middle.

* M5: screw in machine screws of any length as tenting legs. Pad the screw heads so they don’t scratch your desk.
* ¼”-20: the standard camera thread. Users attach super clamps, arms, quick-release plates and similar mounts.

## Care and cleaning

[Section titled “Care and cleaning”](#care-and-cleaning)

Factory builds are printed in tough ABS and handle everyday heat well; like any electronics, don’t leave them in a hot car. Self-printed PLA parts are another matter: they can soften in a hot car, near a heater or in strong sun. ABS dissolves in acetone, so keep acetone away from the board.

* **Keys**: all keys except the finger Center keys lift out. Wash them in cold or room-temperature water with mild soap. Don’t use an ultrasonic cleaner; it heats the water and can warp the keys. Handle the flag on each key carefully.

* **Center keys**: tipping Center keys curl under the cluster to a magnet at the north end. Rotate the key upward to pull its arm off the magnet and out through the cluster.[\*](#older-h-slider)

  ![A finger cluster with its tipping Center key (orange) turned partway up and out, with a curved arrow showing the direction to rotate it.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-remove-line-light.CMGowsEI_ZfvqY8.webp)![A finger cluster with its tipping Center key (orange) turned partway up and out, with a curved arrow showing the direction to rotate it.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-remove-line-dark.BCFXBQVk_Z1KjUWB.webp)![A finger cluster with its tipping Center key (orange) turned partway up and out, with a curved arrow showing the direction to rotate it.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-remove-shaded-light.CqZVN9tt_Z2scWUA.webp)![A finger cluster with its tipping Center key (orange) turned partway up and out, with a curved arrow showing the direction to rotate it.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tipping-remove-shaded-dark.BAxqX2f8_Z1p7l2F.webp)

* **Dust**: blow it out with a powered air duster.

* **Spills**: unplug the board first. Wipe the plastic with a barely damp cloth, keeping water away from the electronics, and let everything dry completely before you plug it back in. Then check that every key still works in [Matrix Tester](/keybard/#check-every-key-with-matrix-tester).

Older builds

1. \* “Gap slider” Center keys pop off the back of the cluster; see the [build guide](https://svalboard.com/build). Don’t lose the sliders. [↩︎](#older-ref-h-slider)

## Opening the case

[Section titled “Opening the case”](#opening-the-case)

1. Turn the half upside down. Don’t rest it on the thumb keys.
2. Remove the seven M3 screws in the bottom plate with the included T10 driver.[\*](#older-h-six-or-seven)
3. Lift off the bottom. You can leave the screws in their holes.

![A half turned upside down and pulled apart: the back cover lifted off the base plate, with seven M3 x 6 mm screws (orange) lined up over its screw holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-back-cover-screws-line-light._E4pBdSr_Z1pcHQa.webp)![A half turned upside down and pulled apart: the back cover lifted off the base plate, with seven M3 x 6 mm screws (orange) lined up over its screw holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-back-cover-screws-line-dark.BNP0Ss3g_Z214NeM.webp)![A half turned upside down and pulled apart: the back cover lifted off the base plate, with seven M3 x 6 mm screws (orange) lined up over its screw holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-back-cover-screws-shaded-light.B_NOih-l_2mmD3j.webp)![A half turned upside down and pulled apart: the back cover lifted off the base plate, with seven M3 x 6 mm screws (orange) lined up over its screw holes.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-back-cover-screws-shaded-dark.DyftLx9Z_2voYW0.webp)

Older builds

1. \* Some older cases have six screws in the bottom plate. [↩︎](#older-ref-h-six-or-seven)

## Self-printing and repairs

[Section titled “Self-printing and repairs”](#self-printing-and-repairs)

* [Build guide](/build/): assembly, print settings, repairs and flashing a new build.
* [Parts repository](https://github.com/svalboard/svalboard-self-print): every plastic part. Customers can request access: send your GitHub username to <morgan@svalboard.com>.
* Ask the community on the [Discord](https://svalboard.com/discord).

## Fit

[Section titled “Fit”](#fit)

Fit matters more than any setting. The tower base screws and cluster height screws are M3 x 6 mm pan head screws with a T10 drive: use the included T10 driver. The [fit video playlist](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ArXnZVQM3LM\&list=PL_Jqu5bq_U_CQBhYryllArikWe-ns3g8q) shows each adjustment.

What moves:

* **Clusters** move up and down on their towers, and roll left and right.
* **Towers** move forward and back, yaw, and slide side to side in the baseplate track.
* **Palm rests** move forward and back, side to side, and yaw.

Some users bend or reverse the steel towers so each cluster sits directly over its tower base.

### Key width

[Section titled “Key width”](#key-width)

Keys should sit as close around your fingers as possible without accidental presses. Print the [sizer sheet](https://www.svalboard.com/sizer) and measure each fingertip, on both hands.

![Four finger clusters cut through the middle, one for each side key size, with a dimension line between the East and West keys: Thick (+1) about 16 mm, Semi (+0.5) about 17 mm, Thin (0) about 18 mm, Backset (−1) about 20 mm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-sizing-line-light.BfWJIKyu_14HKnL.webp)![Four finger clusters cut through the middle, one for each side key size, with a dimension line between the East and West keys: Thick (+1) about 16 mm, Semi (+0.5) about 17 mm, Thin (0) about 18 mm, Backset (−1) about 20 mm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-sizing-line-dark.BDvrYmwP_MQO5z.webp)![Four finger clusters cut through the middle, one for each side key size, with a dimension line between the East and West keys: Thick (+1) about 16 mm, Semi (+0.5) about 17 mm, Thin (0) about 18 mm, Backset (−1) about 20 mm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-sizing-shaded-light.DJFqg6Rj_1Cb1U5.webp)![Four finger clusters cut through the middle, one for each side key size, with a dimension line between the East and West keys: Thick (+1) about 16 mm, Semi (+0.5) about 17 mm, Thin (0) about 18 mm, Backset (−1) about 20 mm.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-key-sizing-shaded-dark.D7nPMC0x_ZRQiHn.webp)

Approximate space between opposite side keys for each key size. The exact gap depends on where you measure it.

Key names give three numbers: **height, thickness, offset**.

* Height: nominal key height in mm.
* Thickness: where the key face sits relative to the front of the key base. +1 is “Thick”, +0.5 “Semi”, 0 “Thin”, −1 “Backset”, −2 “double Backset”. Thicker keys suit narrower fingertips.
* Offset: magnet offset. A larger offset means a lighter press.

| Example  | Meaning                                               |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| 6 1 0.7  | 6 mm tall, Thick, 0.7 mm offset (default, about 20 g) |
| 11 0 0.8 | 11 mm tall, flush, 0.8 mm offset (about 17 g)         |
| 8 −2 1.0 | 8 mm tall, set back 2 mm, 1.0 mm offset (about 12 g)  |

Standard clusters have about 18 mm between key bases. Slim clusters have about 16 mm and need a different circuit board. Your fit is roughly the spacing minus both keys’ thickness:

| Keys   | Cluster | Approximate fit |
| ------ | ------- | --------------- |
| Two +1 | 18 mm   | 16 mm           |
| Two +1 | 16 mm   | 14 mm           |
| Two −1 | 18 mm   | 20 mm           |
| Two −1 | 16 mm   | 18 mm           |

For reference, one user’s measurements and the fits he uses:

|          | L Pinky | L Ring | L Middle | L Index | R Index | R Middle | R Ring | R Pinky |
| -------- | ------- | ------ | -------- | ------- | ------- | -------- | ------ | ------- |
| Measured | 14      | 17     | 16       | 15      | 16      | 16       | 17     | 14      |
| Used     | 16      | 18     | 17       | 17      | 17      | 17       | 18     | 16      |

Include your measurements with your order.

### Trackball size

[Section titled “Trackball size”](#trackball-size)

The default trackball is 44 mm. A 52 mm ball is available for large hands, about 200 mm or more from wrist to middle fingertip. The 44 mm ball gives a more flexible fit even for large hands.

| Size    | Length (wrist to middle fingertip) | Width at knuckles |
| ------- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| X-Small | under 170 mm                       |                   |
| Small   | 170–180 mm                         | under 75 mm       |
| Medium  | 180–190 mm                         | 75–85 mm          |
| Large   | 190–195 mm                         | over 85 mm        |
| X-Large | over 195 mm                        |                   |

![A hand measured from the wrist crease: 180 mm to the middle fingertip and 76 mm across the palm at the knuckles, with the differences between finger lengths marked.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/hand-measurements.Dzi8RokB_ZsUpPe.webp)

### Palm rests

[Section titled “Palm rests”](#palm-rests)

Set the palm rests first. You need a steady hand position before you can fit the clusters.

* Loosen both carrier screws until the carrier moves easily. Tighten until it holds, test, then tighten a little more. Don’t overtighten; it can damage the carrier and base plate.

* With a relaxed hand, your fingers rest on the Center keys. Your base knuckles usually sit just in front of the palm rest’s front edge.

* **Hemispherical palm rests** (default on orders after 2026-09-01): loosen the large center screw slightly with the 3 mm hex key to turn the rest (yaw) and tilt it (pitch and roll), then tighten it firmly. Keep the carriers square to the base plate and set the angle with the rest itself. They ship on 9 mm carriers; other heights are in the parts repository.

  ![A right hemispherical palm rest on its carrier, seen from the front and above. The center screw (orange) sits in the top washer in the middle of the rest, with the window toward the finger clusters. The carrier shows under the rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-assembled-line-light.DADoJfQC_Z1RMUn.webp)![A right hemispherical palm rest on its carrier, seen from the front and above. The center screw (orange) sits in the top washer in the middle of the rest, with the window toward the finger clusters. The carrier shows under the rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-assembled-line-dark.Ciqo8dYJ_Z2s05AL.webp)![A right hemispherical palm rest on its carrier, seen from the front and above. The center screw (orange) sits in the top washer in the middle of the rest, with the window toward the finger clusters. The carrier shows under the rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-assembled-shaded-light.DVtPF_lw_19oUIe.webp)![A right hemispherical palm rest on its carrier, seen from the front and above. The center screw (orange) sits in the top washer in the middle of the rest, with the window toward the finger clusters. The carrier shows under the rest.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-hemi-assembled-shaded-dark.BasL_Puu_1x3i5B.webp)

  The center screw takes the 3 mm hex key.

* **Tripod palm rests**: newer ones have 5 mm shims installed. Remove them to lower the rest 5 mm, or use any shim up to about 6 mm.

  ![Exploded view of a tripod palm rest: the rest at the top, a 5 mm shim (orange) under each of its three legs, the sled with its three leg sockets, and an M2 x 4 mm screw (blue) beside each socket.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tripod-shims-line-light.Cz91DfOj_1tPNSi.webp)![Exploded view of a tripod palm rest: the rest at the top, a 5 mm shim (orange) under each of its three legs, the sled with its three leg sockets, and an M2 x 4 mm screw (blue) beside each socket.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tripod-shims-line-dark.DuncZki-_Z26szQI.webp)![Exploded view of a tripod palm rest: the rest at the top, a 5 mm shim (orange) under each of its three legs, the sled with its three leg sockets, and an M2 x 4 mm screw (blue) beside each socket.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tripod-shims-shaded-light.DCJZ3CUt_fiJ3c.webp)![Exploded view of a tripod palm rest: the rest at the top, a 5 mm shim (orange) under each of its three legs, the sled with its three leg sockets, and an M2 x 4 mm screw (blue) beside each socket.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-tripod-shims-shaded-dark.7ZzLAyre_1aslSP.webp)

  With the 5 mm shims in, the legs sit 5 mm higher and the M2 screws go in the upper holes.
