# USB IDs

> The USB vendor and product IDs each Svalboard firmware uses.

Every Svalboard uses USB vendor ID `303a`. The product ID depends on the firmware release and on the firmware flashed to each half. These tables are generated from the firmware source, so they match the release files.

## Current release

[Section titled “Current release”](#current-release)

`vLaunch2`, released 2026-10-08. Each pointing module has its own firmware, with its own product IDs.

| Firmware                       | Left half | Right half |
| ------------------------------ | --------- | ---------- |
| Base board                     | `4044`    | `4045`     |
| TrackPoint                     | `404a`    | `404b`     |
| PMW3389 trackball              | `4048`    | `4049`     |
| Azoteq touchpad                | `404c`    | `404d`     |
| PMW3360 trackball (deprecated) | `4046`    | `4047`     |

## Linux udev rule

[Section titled “Linux udev rule”](#linux-udev-rule)

On Linux, Keybard needs a udev rule to open the board. One rule covers every product ID above. See [Linux: the udev rule](/firmware/#linux-the-udev-rule).

See [Releases](/reference/releases/) for the firmware files in each release.

# Quickstart

> Set up a new Svalboard, connect it to your computer and check every key.

Your order includes a packing slip. It has a printable keymap of the default layout: [packing slip](http://www.svalboard.com/packing-slip).

1. Insert all thumb keys. The Nail key is mirrored for left and right.

   ![A right thumb cluster seen from its outer side, keys labeled: the Nail and Knuckle keys in front, their sloped tops running together as one line, the layer LED below them, the Pad key behind with its top rising toward the Up key, the Up key, the Down key in the middle, and the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-line-light.DhxyIN4r_RnwvJ.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen from its outer side, keys labeled: the Nail and Knuckle keys in front, their sloped tops running together as one line, the layer LED below them, the Pad key behind with its top rising toward the Up key, the Up key, the Down key in the middle, and the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-line-dark.DDzCwfv7_1Q8N6f.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen from its outer side, keys labeled: the Nail and Knuckle keys in front, their sloped tops running together as one line, the layer LED below them, the Pad key behind with its top rising toward the Up key, the Up key, the Down key in the middle, and the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-shaded-light.DRyMLY9h_27UYIk.webp)![A right thumb cluster seen from its outer side, keys labeled: the Nail and Knuckle keys in front, their sloped tops running together as one line, the layer LED below them, the Pad key behind with its top rising toward the Up key, the Up key, the Down key in the middle, and the cluster body.](/svdocs-r7q2m/_astro/cad-thumb-cluster-keys-shaded-dark.Drw6YBLA_1vTUn.webp)

2. Connect the two halves with a USB-C cable between the ports marked **S** (or **↔**). This is the split cable.

3. Connect one half to your computer with the port marked **U**. This is the main half.

   * If you have a TrackPoint, the TrackPoint half must be the main half.
   * Otherwise, make the half with your main pointing device the main half. The main half performs better.

4. Open [Keybard](https://keybard.svalboard.com) and check every key in its **Matrix Tester** (see [Check every key with Matrix Tester](/keybard/#check-every-key-with-matrix-tester)). On Vial, use Vial’s Matrix Tester (see [The Vial app](/vial/#the-vial-app)).

5. Fit the board to your hands (see [Fit](/hardware/#fit)). Start with the [fit video playlist](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ArXnZVQM3LM\&list=PL_Jqu5bq_U_CQBhYryllArikWe-ns3g8q).

Changes you make in Keybard take effect on the keyboard right away. No flashing needed.

Not sure which firmware your board runs? See [Which firmware](/start/which-firmware/).

# Which firmware

> Find out whether your board runs Svalboard QMK or Svalboard's Vial firmware, and which part of these docs applies.

Svalboard boards run one of two firmwares. Svalboard QMK, configured with Keybard, is the current firmware and the main track of these docs.

|                    | Svalboard QMK (current)                  | Svalboard’s Vial firmware                                                      |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Firmware           | `svalboard/qmk` release vLaunch2         | `svalboard/vial-qmk` release v2025-11-01                                       |
| File names         | `..._sval_vLaunch2.uf2`                  | `..._vial_v2025-11-01.uf2`                                                     |
| Configure with     | Keybard: <https://keybard.svalboard.com> | Vial (<https://vial.rocks> or the desktop app), or the Keybard for Vial boards |
| Layout backup file | `.svil`                                  | `.vil`                                                                         |

## Check your board

[Section titled “Check your board”](#check-your-board)

Open <https://keybard.svalboard.com> in Chrome or Edge and choose **Connect Keyboard**.

* If Keybard shows your layout, you are on Svalboard QMK. See [Keybard](/keybard/) and [What’s new compared with Vial](/firmware/#whats-new-compared-with-vial).
* If Keybard shows **Update your Svalboard’s firmware** and says the board is running Vial firmware, you are on Vial. To update, see [Moving from Vial](/firmware/#moving-from-vial). To stay on Vial, see [Vial firmware](/vial/).

## Svalboard QMK and Keybard

[Section titled “Svalboard QMK and Keybard”](#svalboard-qmk-and-keybard)

Svalboard QMK is the current firmware, `svalboard/qmk`, release **vLaunch2**. You configure it with **Keybard** in your browser. The keyboard stores and runs your setup, so you can close Keybard and keep typing.

Open Keybard at <https://keybard.svalboard.com>.

Keybard needs **Chrome or Edge** on a desktop. Firefox and Safari can’t connect to the keyboard. You can open layout files without a board.

## How these docs are organized

[Section titled “How these docs are organized”](#how-these-docs-are-organized)

* **Hardware**: the halves, fit, typing, pointing modules and troubleshooting. These apply to every Svalboard.
* **Firmware**: flashing, Svalboard QMK files and recovery, and moving between Vial and Svalboard QMK.
* **Keybard**: the configurator, layer lights, and the Keybard Overlay app.
* **Vial**: for boards that stay on Vial.

# Vial firmware

> Svalboard's Vial firmware, for boards that stay on Vial instead of moving to Svalboard QMK.

Svalboard’s Vial firmware is `svalboard/vial-qmk`, release **v2025-11-01**. You configure it with the Vial app, or with the Keybard for Vial boards: <https://captdeaf.github.io/keybard/>

Current Keybard doesn’t edit Vial boards. When it sees Vial firmware, it shows **Update your Svalboard’s firmware**. To move to Svalboard QMK, see [Moving from Vial](/firmware/#moving-from-vial).

## In this section

[Section titled “In this section”](#in-this-section)

* [Vial firmware files](/vial/#vial-firmware-files)
* [Flash Vial firmware](/vial/#flash-vial-firmware)
* [The Vial app](/vial/#the-vial-app)

* [Svalboard keys in Vial](/vial/#svalboard-keys-in-vial)

* [Recovery on Vial](/vial/#recovery-on-vial)

## Vial firmware files

[Section titled “Vial firmware files”](#vial-firmware-files)

Download from the [v2025-11-01 release](https://github.com/svalboard/vial-qmk/releases/tag/v2025-11-01). Pick one file per half, by the module on that half:

| Module on that half                           | Left                                                    | Right                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| None                                          | `svalboard_left_vial_v2025-11-01.uf2`                   | `svalboard_right_vial_v2025-11-01.uf2`                   |
| None, blank keymap (for testing)              | `svalboard_left_blank_v2025-11-01.uf2`                  | `svalboard_right_blank_v2025-11-01.uf2`                  |
| Trackball                                     | `svalboard_trackball_pmw3389_left_vial_v2025-11-01.uf2` | `svalboard_trackball_pmw3389_right_vial_v2025-11-01.uf2` |
| TrackPoint                                    | `svalboard_trackpoint_left_vial_v2025-11-01.uf2`        | `svalboard_trackpoint_right_vial_v2025-11-01.uf2`        |
| Touchpad                                      | `svalboard_azoteq_left_vial_v2025-11-01.uf2`            | `svalboard_azoteq_right_vial_v2025-11-01.uf2`            |
| Trackball, early 2024 units only (deprecated) | `svalboard_trackball_pmw3360_left_vial_v2025-11-01.uf2` | `svalboard_trackball_pmw3360_right_vial_v2025-11-01.uf2` |

Early alpha units (before July 2023): contact <support@svalboard.com>.

## Flash Vial firmware

[Section titled “Flash Vial firmware”](#flash-vial-firmware)

1. In Vial, save your layout: **File → Save current layout** (`.vil`). Flashing resets the layout to the default.
2. Flash both halves as in [Flashing firmware](/firmware/#flashing-firmware), with the files from [Vial firmware files](/vial/#vial-firmware-files).
3. Open Vial. It connects by itself; it may take a couple of tries.
4. **File → Load saved layout** and choose your `.vil`.

After flashing:

* The mouse-layer timeout resets to its default, 500 ms. See [Pointing settings in Vial](/vial/#pointing-settings-in-vial).
* Vial stores the keymap on each half separately. If you plug the computer into the other half, the layout can look different. Load your `.vil` again.

## The Vial app

[Section titled “The Vial app”](#the-vial-app)

* Web: <https://vial.rocks> (Chrome or Edge).
* Desktop: <https://get.vial.today>.

Edits are live: change a key and it changes on the keyboard. Useful parts:

* **Matrix Tester** tab: press each key to check it registers.
* **File → Save current layout / Load saved layout**: `.vil` backups.
* Community layouts for Vial: [svalboard-configs](https://github.com/svalboard/svalboard-configs). Load one with **File → Load saved layout**.

## Layers, tap dances, combos, overrides and macros

[Section titled “Layers, tap dances, combos, overrides and macros”](#layers-tap-dances-combos-overrides-and-macros)

Vial edits these directly:

* **Layers**: assign layer keys (MO, LT, TG, TT, OSL, TO, DF) like any key. Layer 15 is the mouse layer; keep it last.
* **Tap dances**: up to 50.
* **Combos**: up to 50.
* **Key overrides**: up to 30.
* **Macros**: up to 50.
* **QMK settings**: tapping term and other timing.

Layer light colors are set in the firmware, with the same defaults as Svalboard QMK (see [Layer lights and brightness](/keybard/#layer-lights-and-brightness)): green for layer 0, orange for layer 1, azure for layer 2, magenta for layer 15. Vial can’t change them.

## Svalboard keys in Vial

[Section titled “Svalboard keys in Vial”](#svalboard-keys-in-vial)

Svalboard’s keys are in Vial’s **User** tab. Bind them anywhere in your layout.

| Key                                      | What it does                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Left / Right DPI + and −                 | Pointer speed per side: 200, 400, 800, 1200, 1600, 2400. Doesn’t wrap. Saved. Not for the TrackPoint. |
| Sniper 2x / 3x / 5x                      | Hold for slower pointing. Works on all pointers. Holding two multiplies them.                         |
| Scroll Left Toggle / Scroll Right Toggle | Switch that side between pointing and scrolling. Saved.                                               |
| Scroll Toggle                            | Switch both sides until you press it again or restart.                                                |
| Scroll Toggle Hold                       | Switch both sides while held.                                                                         |
| AutoMouse Toggle                         | Turn the automatic mouse layer off or on. Saved.                                                      |
| Mouse Key Timer                          | Cycle the mouse-layer timeout: 200, 300, 400, 500, 800 ms, no timeout. Default 500 ms. Saved.         |
| Fix Drift                                | Recalibrate a TrackPoint. Keep your finger off it.                                                    |
| Toggle ACH                               | Turn Achordion on or off. Saved.                                                                      |
| Caps Word Toggle                         | Capitalize one word. `-` becomes `_`.                                                                 |
| MO 23 45=67 and MO 45 23=67              | Hold to turn on layers 2 and 3, or 4 and 5. Hold both for 6 and 7.                                    |
| Output Status                            | Types the firmware version, pointer settings, Achordion and timer state.                              |

Keys marked “Saved” can’t go on the mouse layer. This protects the keyboard’s settings memory from repeated writes.

### Achordion

[Section titled “Achordion”](#achordion)

**Achordion** stops same-hand rolls from triggering mod-tap modifiers. By default a mod-tap only acts as a modifier with a key on the other hand, unless you hold it about one second.

### Mod-tap with any tap key

[Section titled “Mod-tap with any tap key”](#mod-tap-with-any-tap-key)

If a mod-tap’s tap key is Transparent, it sends the key from the next active layer below, even a shifted symbol. Both layers must be active.

More detail: [Svalboard advanced features](https://github.com/svalboard/vial-qmk/blob/vial/keyboards/svalboard/docs/non_standard_firmware_features.md).

## Pointing settings in Vial

[Section titled “Pointing settings in Vial”](#pointing-settings-in-vial)

* **Timeout**: bind Mouse Key Timer (see [Svalboard keys in Vial](/vial/#svalboard-keys-in-vial)) and press it to cycle.
* **Turn off automouse**: bind AutoMouse Toggle and press it once.
* **Edit the mouse layer**: edit layer 15. On the Vial default mouse layer, Pinky Center is Fix Drift.
* **Speed**: DPI keys per side; Sniper keys while held.
* **Scrolling**: Scroll Left/Right Toggle to set each side; Scroll Toggle or Scroll Toggle Hold to switch for a moment.
* **TrackPoint drift**: Fix Drift. If drift persists, a larger dead zone needs a custom firmware build; ask on the [Discord](https://svalboard.com/discord).

Full reference: [pointing devices guide](https://svalboard.com/scroll). For the modules themselves, see [Pointing modules](/hardware/#pointing-modules).

## Recovery on Vial

[Section titled “Recovery on Vial”](#recovery-on-vial)

* **A drive named RPI-RP2 appeared**: the half is in bootloader mode. Press RESET once.
* **Layout looks wrong or reset**: load your `.vil` with **File → Load saved layout**.
* **Layout differs depending on which half is plugged in**: load your `.vil` while plugged into the half you use.
* **Board won’t start after flashing**: reflash both halves with matching files from the same release (see [Flashing firmware](/firmware/#flashing-firmware)).

For hardware problems, see [Troubleshooting](/hardware/#troubleshooting).
